articles.title: 70 Americans still unaccounted for after catastrophic Nepal flooding
articles.excerpt:
Fox News correspondent Stephanie Bennett reports on rescue operations in Nepal following a glacier collapse that triggered flash flooding.

The State Department said Tuesday it is aware of approximate...
articles.body_text:
Fox News correspondent Stephanie Bennett reports on rescue operations in Nepal following a glacier collapse that triggered flash flooding.

The State Department said Tuesday it is aware of approximately 70 Americans who remain unaccounted for in the Nepal-China border region following last month's catastrophic flooding, while 18 Americans have now made it to safety.

"We extend our deepest sympathy to all those affected by the flooding in Nepal, and their families, and we reaffirm our enduring friendship with the Nepali people," a State Department official told Fox News.

"The Department of State remains in close contact with the families of Americans who remain unaccounted for and is committed to providing regular updates as more information becomes available."

ROUGHLY 80 AMERICANS STILL UNACCOUNTED FOR AFTER HIMALAYAN DISASTER KILLS 903, OFFICIALS SAY

Heavy machinery clears a road along the Trishuli River after deadly flash floods and mudslides in Nuwakot district, Bagmati province, Nepal, on Sept. 8, 2026. (REUTERS/Anushree Fadnavis)

Officials also urged Americans not to travel to the disaster zone, warning the region remains at risk for additional flash floods and landslides.

The latest update reduced the number of Americans unaccounted for from 75 to 70, while the number confirmed safe rose from 16 to 18.

Officials have not confirmed any American deaths.

RESCUERS USE ZIPLINES TO TRANSPORT TRAPPED CITIZENS AFTER DEVASTATING NEPAL FLOODS DECIMATE COUNTRY'S BRIDGES

A flooded home is seen after deadly flash floods and mudslides devastated Nuwakot district, Nepal, on Sept. 8, 2026. (REUTERS/Anushree Fadnavis)

As search efforts continue, Nepalese authorities said rescuers are concentrating on three hydropower project tunnels where they believe dozens of workers may still be trapped beneath debris left by the Aug. 26 glacier collapse that triggered devastating flooding along the Nepal-China border, according to Reuters.

"Our search operation is focused on finding survivors, including in tunnels. Our bigger focus is on the Chilime hydroelectric project, where we believe people are trapped, because there was a canteen, residency and arrangements for food," Dharma Raj Upreti, chief of Nepal's disaster authority, told Reuters.

DEATH TOLL FROM MUDSLIDES, FLOODING AT NEPAL-CHINA BORDER CLIMBS PAST 670; NEARLY 3,000 MISSING

Damaged homes line the banks of the Trishuli River after deadly flash floods and mudslides in Nuwakot district, Nepal, on Sept. 8, 2026. (REUTERS/Anushree Fadnavis)

The disaster has killed at least 1,399 people across Nepal and China's Tibet region, with more than 5,400 others still missing, according to authorities.

Both governments have blamed climate change for the glacier collapse that unleashed the flooding.

Sophia Compton is a Writer at Fox News Digital. Sophia was previously a business reporter covering finance, energy and tourism and has experience as a TV news producer. She graduated with a journalism degree in 2021 from the University of Hawaii at Manoa. Story tips can be sent to sophia.compton@fox.com.

articles.title: 'The View' co-host demands 25th Amendment be used against Trump, suggests Cabinet could do it after midterms
articles.excerpt:
Sunny Hostin called for the 25th Amendment to be used against President Donald Trump on Tuesday, suggesting it could be done by the Cabinet if Republicans lose control of Congress.

"The View" co-host...
articles.body_text:
Sunny Hostin called for the 25th Amendment to be used against President Donald Trump on Tuesday, suggesting it could be done by the Cabinet if Republicans lose control of Congress.

"The View" co-host Sunny Hostin raised using the 25th Amendment against President Donald Trump on Tuesday, as the ABC talk show returned from its summer break.

"My question is when do we really start, in earnest — and I mean this honestly — considering the 25th Amendment," Hostin said.

"I think when the Republicans lose the House, and they lose the Senate, they’re going to want to have some control over this person, this person that is in the office, and JD Vance would then be that replacement and I wonder if the Cabinet then looks at each other and says, okay, we’ve got to take control of this, 25th Amendment," she added.

The 25th Amendment to the Constitution empowers a president’s Cabinet to remove him from office if he is unable to do the job.

PUSH TO OUST TRUMP EXPOSES CRACKS AMONG DEMOCRATS ON STRATEGY, TIMING

Co-host Sunny Hostin speaks during ABC's "The View" on July 6, 2026. (ABC/TheView)

Co-host Alyssa Farah Griffin pushed back, saying she didn't think Trump's Cabinet would ever take such action.

"I think if they didn’t do it after January 6, in that period before he left office [in 2021], it’s never going to happen," she said.

The White House did not immediately return Fox News Digital's request for comment.

Co-hosts Whoopi Goldberg and Joy Behar have also called for the use of the 25th Amendment against Trump since he returned to office last year.

JEN PSAKI SHUTS DOWN 25TH AMENDMENT TALK ABOUT TRUMP, DECLARES IT'S 'NOT GOING TO HAPPEN'

While criticizing Trump's efforts to resolve the war between Russia and Ukraine in September 2025, Goldberg said, "He had an opportunity to do so much more than he offered them, and they don’t consider him to be serious anymore, and I’m worried. What is the amendment, the 20-"

The co-hosts took their guesses at which amendment Goldberg was referencing, making multiple attempts before Hostin eventually informed them that it was the 25th Amendment.

"They questioned Biden’s competence," Goldberg said at the time. "If Biden had acted like this, I would have said take him and sit him down somewhere, but this was not — this was not presidential, and this was not helpful."

After Trump unveiled plaques beneath portraits of his predecessors, including Barack Obama and Joe Biden, on the new White House Presidential Walk of Fame in December 2025, Behar asked when the Cabinet would push to remove the president.

"When are they going to invoke the 25th Amendment? Does he have to run naked into the White House or what? What is that amendment for if not for this?" Behar said, drawing laughter from the audience.

FCC CHAIR MOCKS 'THE VIEW' HOST SUNNY HOSTIN FOR BLATANT PARTISANSHIP AS SHE PLEADS FOR DEMS TO WIN SENATE

"The View" launched a campaign seeking public support in June amid a Federal Communications Commission (FCC) investigation into the liberal talk show as the agency cracks down on equal time for political candidates after Texas Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico joined the co-hosts for an interview.

ABC’s campaign features a petition to declare that "The View" qualifies as a bona fide news interview program. A commercial debuted in June during the program that declared, "’The View has welcomed your favorite guests for nearly 30 years. Now the FCC wants to control who is allowed to appear on the show. Tell the FCC to let the viewers decide."

Hanna Panreck is an associate editor at Fox News.

articles.title: Erik and Lyle Menendez eligible to face parole board early next year
articles.excerpt:
Brothers, convicted of parents’ killings and denied parole last year, permitted to apply for another hearing earlier than expected

Erik and Lyle Menendez will be before a parole board again in March,...
articles.body_text:
Brothers, convicted of parents’ killings and denied parole last year, permitted to apply for another hearing earlier than expected

Erik and Lyle Menendez will be before a parole board again in March, about 17 months earlier than expected.

The brothers were originally sentenced in 1996 to life in prison for the 1989 fatal shootings of their father, Jose Menendez, and mother, Kitty Menendez, in their Beverly Hills mansion. A Los Angeles judge reduced their sentences to 50 years to life in May 2025, making them eligible for parole because they were under age 26 when they committed their crimes.

They were denied parole in August 2025, with the California parole board saying Lyle Menendez still displayed “anti-social personality traits like deception” and that Erik Menendez broke prison rules by repeatedly using a cellphone.

The brothers were then eligible to apply for another hearing in August 2028. That has now been tentatively moved up to March by the parole board after the brothers’ requests for earlier hearings were granted on Friday.

The California department of corrections and rehabilitation allows eligible prisoners to seek earlier parole if there is “a change in circumstances or new information indicating the person may be suitable for parole”.

The department did not immediately respond to requests for comment about why the brothers were granted an earlier hearing. The brothers’ attorney declined to comment through a family spokeswoman.

The case has long captivated true crime enthusiasts, with the brothers amassing public support in recent years after shows on Netflix renewed interest.

Weeks after the board rejected their release last year, a Los Angeles judge denied their petition seeking a review of their convictions based on new evidence supporting their claims of sexual abuse by their father.

“For almost 40 years, Erik and Lyle have worked to take responsibility for their actions, confront and heal from the unimaginable abuse and trauma they endured, grow as individuals, and dedicate themselves to serving others,” their family said in a statement on Monday.

The family said the brothers, who are in a San Diego prison, helped establish a hospice program and created a beautification program at the prison.

“They have sought to build an environment that reminds people serving life sentences that their lives still have meaning and that, regardless of their circumstances, they can choose each day to grow, heal, accept accountability,” the family said.

The brothers went on trial separately, and in 1994 each jury deadlocked. Prosecutors argued that they killed their parents for financial gain. The brothers’ attorneys did not dispute the pair killed their parents but argued that they acted out of self-defense after years of emotional and sexual abuse by their father.

Two years later, the brothers were retried together with much of the defense evidence about alleged sexual abuse excluded. Jurors convicted both brothers of first-degree murder.

articles.title: Spanish FA launches fertility support for female players and referees
articles.excerpt: Spain’s football federation has unveiled an agreement to support fertility treatment for female players and referees, presenting the measure as another way to give women in elite football greater free...
articles.body_text:
Spain’s football federation has unveiled an agreement to support fertility treatment for female players and referees, presenting the measure as another way to give women in elite football greater freedom to decide if and when to become mothers.

The Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) said on Tuesday its agreement with the Tambre clinic would allow sportswomen to access treatments including in vitro fertilisation and egg freezing, in what the federation called a pioneering step for women’s sport in the country.

Spain internationals Olga Carmona and Patri Guijarro attended the announcement and welcomed the deal as an important tool for players managing the demands of professional sport and personal life.

“We are very happy to have reached this agreement, to have one more option to decide how and when to choose to become a mother,” Carmona said.

Guijarro said the measure formed part of a broader push to improve work-life balance for female athletes and ensure motherhood does not become a barrier to a career in elite sport.

“Ultimately, it’s a very positive agreement because it’s true that for all these years we’ve been fighting to achieve a better work-life balance for mothers,” Guijarro said.

“In the case of being able to have a career whilst being a mother, work-life balance measures are now being put in place; we feel we’ve been listened to. It’s important that female athletes feel they don’t have to choose between their professional and personal lives.”

According to Reyes Bellver Alonso, director of women’s football at the RFEF, the federation will cover the full cost of egg-freezing treatment and provide a range of benefits linked to different treatments for all international players who have been called up at least twice. The deal with Tambre will be in place until 2029.

“The debate on motherhood and work-life balance is a vast one, and it is good that these issues are being discussed because it always helps to raise their profile in other areas,” Bellver Alonso said.

She said football had made significant progress in protecting players’ rights, contracts and pregnancy safeguards, including eliminating anti-pregnancy clauses.

“If there is one area where work has been done on maternity rights, the protection of women, the protection of contracts and work-life balance in women’s sport, it is football,” she said.

“I think that we often focus on the criticism and fail to convey how beneficial and pioneering these developments are, and the struggles the players have also gone through.”

The RFEF said the agreement was not designed to discourage footballers from having children while they are active, but to offer another option so they do not have to rule out motherhood because of their sporting career.

It said the initiative complements existing work-life balance measures, including support that allows players who have become mothers to have their children close by during away trips, training camps and tournaments.

The announcement has also prompted debate among labour and equality organisations in Spain, with some warning that fertility support should not replace stronger workplace protections for mothers.

Olympic bronze medallist and triple jumper Ana Peleteiro described the measure as “deeply sexist” in a video posted on social media, while the CCOO trade union said the focus should remain on work-life balance and protecting pregnancy during competition.

articles.title: Sabalenka holds off Noskova to keep US Open three-peat bid alive
articles.excerpt:
Two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka rallied in the final set to beat Linda Noskova in a match tiebreaker on Tuesday and reach a sixth straight US Open semifinal.

Sabalenka triumphed 7-6 (7/1)...
articles.body_text:
Two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka rallied in the final set to beat Linda Noskova in a match tiebreaker on Tuesday and reach a sixth straight US Open semifinal.

Sabalenka triumphed 7-6 (7/1), 3-6, 7-6 (10/7) over the 21-year-old Wimbledon champion, striking 42 winners but converting just two of her nine break point chances against the resilient Czech in a fierce duel on Arthur Ashe Stadium.

Trailing 4-2 in the third, Sabalenka appeared headed for another Grand Slam disappointment in a season in which she has so far been unable to add to her stash of four major titles.

Clearly frustrated, Sabalenka nevertheless regrouped and broke Noskova to love to pull level at 4-4. They hurtled to the tiebreaker — where Sabalenka dropped the first two points before climbing back and finally sealed victory with a courageous second-serve ace.

Noskova fired 18 aces — 46 winners in all — as she became the first player to take a set off Sabalenka in the tournament.

“What a battle,” Sabalenka said. “I was pushing myself to the limit in this match especially in the third set.

“I honestly thought the match was over and that’s what helped me to feel loose and go for my shots.”

Sabalenka has now won 18 straight matches at Flushing Meadows, and she must keep going to a third straight title if she is to have a chance to retain the world number one ranking she has held since October of 2024.

The victory was Sabalenka’s first win over a top-10 player since she beat Coco Gauff in the Miami final in March.

That was her third title of 2026, but Sabalenka has struggled since, exiting early at both Roland Garros and Wimbledon.

The Belarusian will next face the winner of the all-American quarterfinal between third seed Jessica Pegula and Emma Navarro.

Pegula is among the trio of players who arrived at Flushing Meadows with a chance to seize Sabalenka’s number one ranking.

A two-time winner on the WTA tour this year, 2024 finalist Pegula would have to win he first Grand Slam title to have a shot at the top spot.

She reached the US Open final in 2024 and owns a 4-0 career record over 26th-seeded Navarro.

Men’s defending champion Carlos Alcaraz faces his toughest test of the tournament, taking on eighth-seeded American Ben Shelton for a place in the semifinals.

Shelton expects to face a full-strength Alcaraz despite the fact that the seven-time Grand Slam champion is playing his first tournament in more than four months after recovering from a right wrist injury.

Alcaraz, who completed a career Grand Slam with his Australian Open triumph in January, has improved with every match and will likely need to do so again against Shelton, who is the leading contender to end American men’s 23-year Grand Slam title drought.

Two more Americans face off in Tuesday’s other men’s quarterfinal, with charismatic 11th seed Frances Tiafoe taking on 22-year-old Alex Michelsen.

articles.title: Trump's unusual role at midterm convention revealed as schedule goes public
articles.excerpt:
House Speaker Mike Johnson previews the GOP midterm convention, saying in a Fox News Digital interview that it will ‘animate’ Republican voters.

EXCLUSIVE — DALLAS — With an eye toward energizing the...
articles.body_text:
House Speaker Mike Johnson previews the GOP midterm convention, saying in a Fox News Digital interview that it will ‘animate’ Republican voters.

EXCLUSIVE — DALLAS — With an eye toward energizing the GOP's MAGA base, the Republican National Committee (RNC) on Tuesday announced the speaking order and times of this week's first-ever GOP midterm convention, and President Donald Trump will be the Primetime headliner both nights.

According to the list, which was shared first with Fox News Digital on the eve of the convention, the president will deliver Wednesday's keynote address, which is tentatively scheduled to start at 9 p.m. ET.

Trump will return on Thursday evening at the American Airlines Center in downtown Dallas to close out the convention, with remarks after Vice President JD Vance gives the second night's keynote speech.

With less than two months to go until the midterm elections, Trump and Republicans are gathering in Texas for their historic confab as they aim to energize the party's base ahead of key races that will determine whether the GOP keeps control of Congress. Supporters of the president traditionally do not turn out in robust numbers when Trump is not on the ballot.

DEMOCRACY ’26: STAY UP TO DATE WITH THE FOX NEWS ELECTION HUB

President Donald Trump, seen at campaign rally for Sen. Darline Graham at Myrtle Beach Convention Center in Myrtle Beach, S.C. on Aug. 21, 2026, will speak in primetime Wednesday and Thursday at the GOP's midterm convention. (SAUL LOEB / AFP via Getty Images)

Democrats and Republicans traditionally hold large nominating conventions during presidential election years. But Trump last year floated the idea of a similar gathering ahead of the midterms to showcase the signature policy achievements he and Republicans in Congress have produced over the past two years.

The president called the convention "a truly Historic Event" and "a RALLY like none other!" when he announced it earlier this summer.

The convention comes as Republicans face energized Democrats and stiff political headwinds as they defend their slim House and Senate majorities in the midterms.

But Republicans are expected to paint a contrast, as they use the convention to spotlight the Democrats' leftward lurch and tie the entire Democratic Party to far-left and socialist proposals.

"The midterm election is about the future of our country. President Donald Trump and Republicans are fighting to launch the golden age of America while extreme liberal Democrats want to tear this country apart and create a liberal failed state with their out-of-touch and anti-American views,"," Republican National Committee chair Joe Gruters argued in a statement to Fox News Digital.

THESE 12 MIDTERM RACES WILL DECIDE WHICH PARTY CONTROLS THE SENATE

Gruters emphasized that "the choice is clear in November and the American people will reject these liberal policies and deliver historic wins for Republicans across the country."

The DNC, which remains in debt and decided against holding a similar convention, sees the GOP confab as a chance to blast Republicans.

"While everyday Americans struggle to pay their bills, fill up their tanks, or put food on the table, Republicans are hosting a multi-million dollar celebration to satisfy an aging and erratic Trump and tie vulnerable Republican candidates closer to his failed agenda,"," DNC Rapid Response Director Kendall Witmer charged.

Witmer argued that "Americans don’t want a ‘Trumpapalooza’ — they want lower costs and affordable healthcare."

The convention will also serve as the GOP's closing argument heading into November. In the fight for the Senate majority, Republican candidates in some of the most crucial races will also address the convention.

Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, the GOP nominee in Texas who is facing off against Democratic state Rep. James Talarico in the race to replace Republican Sen. John Cornyn, will speak on the first evening. So will former RNC Chair Mike Whatley, who is defending retiring GOP Sen. Thom Tillis' seat in battleground North Carolina.

Ken Paxton, Texas attorney general and Republican US Senate candidate, arrives to speak during a runoff election night event in Plano, Texas, US, on Tuesday, May 26, 2026. (Antranik Tavitian/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Sen. Jon Husted of Ohio, who is in a pitched fight with former longtime Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown, will also address the crowd, as will Rep. Mike Collins of Georgia, the Republican challenger taking on Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff in swing state Georgia.

Former Rep. Mike Rogers of Michigan, who is hoping to flip a Democrat-held open seat in the key Great Lakes battleground as he runs against far-left Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed, speaks on Thursday evening.

In the battle for the House, where the GOP holds a razor-thin majority, incumbents and candidates in competitive races will also be in the speaking spotlight.

They include Reps. Monica De La Cruz of Texas, Derrick Van Orden of Wisconsin, Rob Bresnahan of Pennsylvania, and candidates Mike LiPetri of New York and Jay Feely of Arizona on Wednesday night.

Among the House Republican incumbents and candidates in close races speaking on Thursday are Reps. Ryan Mackenzie of Pennsylvania and Mike Lawler of New York, along with nominees Greg Cunningham of New Mexico, Derrick Merrin of Ohio and Eric Flores of Texas.

STATE OF PLAY: WHO'S UP AND WHO'S DOWN IN THE LATEST FOX NEWS POWER RANKINGS

The American Airlines Center, as preparations are underway for the Republican National Midterm Convention in Dallas, Texas, U.S., September 7, 2026 ( )

Speaker Mike Johnson will speak on Thursday evening, according to the RNC schedule.

Johnson's Senate counterpart, Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-South Dakota), is notably absent from the list of speakers released by the RNC. But a source familiar with the planning tells Fox News Digital that Thune will be in Dallas, with a full schedule that includes helping Senate candidates fundraise.

Texas Gov. Greg Abbott, who is running for a fourth term leading the Lone Star State, speaks on Thursday. So does Sen. Ted Cruz of Texas, the conservative firebrand who is not on the ballot this year but could make a second White House bid in 2028.

Meanwhile, some of the biggest names in Trump's Cabinet are scheduled to speak, including Attorney General Todd Blanche and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Wednesday evening, and Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., who spearheaded the Make America Healthy Again (MAHA) movement, on Thursday evening.

Paul Steinhauser covers the national campaign trail from coast to coast for Fox News

articles.title: Virginia county to pay up to $2K to families with primary wage earner detained by ICE
articles.excerpt: Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents arrest more than 1,300 illegal immigrants in a massive Washington, D.C. area sweep known as Operation Safe Community. 'Fox & Friends' co-hosts break do...
articles.body_text:
Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents arrest more than 1,300 illegal immigrants in a massive Washington, D.C. area sweep known as Operation Safe Community. 'Fox & Friends' co-hosts break down the arrests of MS-13 gang members and a suspect tied to student fentanyl overdoses. The operation highlights growing concerns over border security and local community safety.

Leaders in one Virginia county approved a program last week to set aside $50,000 to support families in which the primary wage earner has been detained by federal immigration authorities.

In a special Sept. 2 meeting, the Arlington County Board voted 4-0 to appropriate the funds, which will be distributed by Arlington Thrive, which describes itself as a "key component of the social safety net" in partnership with the county government.

Under the program, eligible families will receive up to $2,000 for those who have lost the primary wage earner. Arlington Thrive aims to assist between 25 to 30 families, according to the board's agenda.

HOW GUARANTEED INCOME ADVOCATES STRIVE TO TURN CASH ASSISTANCE INTO POLICY AFTER COVID-RELIEF FUNDS DRIED UP

Federal immigration authorities make an arrest in Arlington, Va., in February. Arlington County leaders recently voted to set aside $50,000 to give families up to $2,000 if the primary wage earner was detained by immigration authorities. (ICE)

"We stand with our immigrant families, and we will not stop doing so," Board Chair Matt de Ferranti said. "We are valuing the families of those that have been displaced and removed."

The move was in response to the Trump administration's illegal immigration enforcement efforts in the Washington, D.C., area in recent months.

"Ensuring that we take care of our community and our residents and our people does mean making sure that we have emergency assistance available for what is probably one of the most challenging situations that you could possibly face," Board Vice Chair Maureen Coffey said. "I'm very proud of us for doing this."

SANCTUARY COUNTY REFUSED 615 ICE TRANSFER REQUESTS, TURNED OVER JUST 11 ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS, RECORDS SHOW

Arlington County Board of Supervisors (from left to right): Julius D. "JD" Spain, Sr., Susan Cunningham, Takis Karantonis, Board Chair Matt de Ferranti and Vice Chair Maureen Coffey. (Arlington County)

The funds will be distributed to families in the form of debit cards and checks.

Elizabeth Matlock, a staff member in the county manager’s office who is coordinating the effort, said the organization is ready to begin issuing funds.

"Thrive is eager to get started with this project," she said.

The vote came as officers with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) quietly made more than 1,300 arrests of illegal immigrants over 14 days in the Washington, D.C., suburbs last month.

Of those arrested, almost 400 illegal immigrants had criminal convictions or pending criminal charges, including a Salvadoran national wanted in Richmond, Virginia, on a murder warrant. Other crimes included rape, sexual assault, kidnapping, DUI, robbery and attempted murder.

Louis Casiano is a reporter for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to louis.casiano@fox.com.

Travelers heading to high-risk destinations should prepare for emergencies, as estate planning attorney Allison Marketti discusses the wills and powers of attorney adults should have in place.

Americ...
articles.body_text:
Travelers heading to high-risk destinations should prepare for emergencies, as estate planning attorney Allison Marketti discusses the wills and powers of attorney adults should have in place.

Americans who may be planning a trip to China are urged to take extra precautions, as U.S. officials warn travelers to "keep a low profile" while visiting the country.

The State Department recently updated its Level 2 "Exercise Increased Caution" advisory for mainland China, warning Americans about the arbitrary enforcement of local laws, exit bans and "the risk of unjust arrest or detention."

U.S. citizens could be questioned or detained without being told what crime they are accused of — and without being given access to U.S. consular services, according to the advisory.

AMERICANS HEADED FOR HIGH-RISK NATION URGED TO PREPARE WILLS, LEAVE DNA SAMPLES AHEAD OF TIME

"U.S. citizens in China may also face interrogations and detention without fair and transparent treatment under the law," the State Department warns.

The advisory notes that business people, academics and journalists are among those who have faced questioning, detention or expulsion for alleged violations of China's national security laws.

The U.S. government is urging Americans who are traveling to China to take extra precautions and "keep a low profile" while visiting the country. (VCG via Getty Images)

"U.S. citizens might only become aware of an exit ban when they attempt to depart China," the advisory states.

The State Department said the restrictions have been used to pressure people to participate in investigations, resolve civil disputes and compel relatives or associates to return to China.

In some cases, exit bans have remained in place for years, preventing U.S. citizens from leaving the country even to receive medical treatment, according to the advisory.

Officials are also warning Americans to be careful about what they say and share electronically while traveling.

The State Department recently updated its Level 2 "Exercise Increased Caution" advisory for mainland China. (iStock)

"Assume that China's security services can read your emails, texts, and social media posts if you send them to or from China," the advisory states.

The State Department warns that Americans could be detained or deported for private electronic messages critical of China, Hong Kong, Macau or the Chinese Communist Party.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Authorities have detained people over messages sent while they were outside China, according to the advisory.

For Americans who decide to travel to mainland China, officials recommend avoiding demonstrations and being cautious around large gatherings.

The U.S. State Department warns that Americans could be detained or deported for private electronic messages critical of China, Hong Kong, Macau or the Chinese Communist Party. (Xinhua News Agency via Getty Images)

Travelers are also advised to avoid sharing opinions either publicly or privately that Chinese authorities could consider embarrassing or negative and to avoid photographing protesters or police without permission.

"Keep a low profile," the State Department advises.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The updated advisory also includes separate guidance for Hong Kong and Macau.

Americans are advised to exercise increased caution in Hong Kong due to the arbitrary enforcement of local laws.

Macau carries a higher Level 3 "Reconsider Travel" advisory due to similar concerns and the U.S. government's limited ability to provide emergency consular services there.

Fox News Digital reached out to the State Department for comment and further information.

Kelly McGreal is a production assistant with the lifestyle team at Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Burning Man deaths this year triple the average as attendee age at Nevada’s desert festival ticks upward
articles.excerpt:
More attendees are in their 40s and 50s, with fewer festival-goers in their 20s

Three people died at Burning Man this year, tripling the average number of deaths in connection with the annual festiva...
articles.body_text:
More attendees are in their 40s and 50s, with fewer festival-goers in their 20s

Three people died at Burning Man this year, tripling the average number of deaths in connection with the annual festival that brings tens of thousands of people to build a temporary utopian community in the brutal conditions of the Nevada desert.

The increase in fatalities comes as news reports have highlighted that the average age of Burning Man attendees is increasing, with fewer participants in their 20s, and more in their 40s and 50s.

“Although we average one death a year at the festival, we have had two so far this year within the confines of the festival and I have received information regarding a third who died in transit to a hospital in Reno,” the Pershing county sheriff, Jerry Allen, told the Reno Gazette-Journal.

The festival, which has attracted upwards of 70,000 people in recent years, ended on 7 September. Founded in San Francisco in 1986 as a genuinely countercultural event, in which local artists built effigies and then set them on fire, Burning Man has increasingly become a jet-setting destination for the global tech elite.

Data from the annual Black Rock City census found that the estimated number of Burning Man participants in their 20s dropped from about 30% of total attendees in 2014, to only 10% in 2025, while the percentage of attendees in their 40s and 50s rose.

The first person who died this year was a man in his “mid-50s”, and the second was a 60 year-old man, the San Francisco Chronicle reported. Allen’s office confirmed that there were no signs of foul play with the first two deaths, both of which occurred at the festival held in the Black Rock playa, an arid stretch of federally managed land about 120 miles from Reno.

Last year, a 37-year old man was found dead in a pool of blood on the final day of the festival, in what authorities said they were investigating as a homicide. The case, which was the festival’s first known homicide in nearly four decades, remains unsolved, the Reno Gazette-Journal reported.

The Burning Man Organization did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the three deaths this year.

The Pershing county sheriff’s office said this year’s first death was reported in the early evening of 3 September, at Rampart, the temporary hospital in the festival’s Black Rock City. A man had been found on the street within the festival and had been given CPR for several minutes before a doctor pronounced him deceased, the sheriff’s office said. The second death was reported in the afternoon of the 5 September, when a man was reported to have been found deceased in his trailer he was sharing with his significant other.

More information on the deaths will be available in approximately six to eight weeks, after autopsies and toxicology reports are completed, the Pershing county sheriff’s office said in a statement. That office referred all questions about the third Burning Man-related death this year to Washoe county, where the county medical examiner’s office did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

articles.title: Government land-grab agenda hits key Senate race as Dem backs property takeovers echoing Mamdani
articles.excerpt: Former Maine Senate President Troy Jackson, D-Fort Kent, told a crowd at the Blueberry Ridge Mobile Village in Wells, Maine, that action should be taken against landlords for substandard utilities and...
articles.body_text:
Former Maine Senate President Troy Jackson, D-Fort Kent, told a crowd at the Blueberry Ridge Mobile Village in Wells, Maine, that action should be taken against landlords for substandard utilities and conditions.

Graham Platner’s replacement in the Maine Senate race suggested the government should be able to take over private property when necessary, appearing to echo socialist New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s housing agenda.

Troy Jackson, a Democrat running for the Senate, came under fire for suggesting the government should be able to take over private property when necessary. The comments drew fresh scrutiny to a candidate the Pine Tree State’s GOP chair previously dubbed "Maine’s Mamdani" to Fox News Digital, as debates over government intervention in housing and private ownership gain new attention.

"It’s a major issue. The greed that's happening right now in this country that people in mobile home parks are feeling is like something I've never seen," Jackson told a small crowd of residents at Blueberry Ridge Mobile Village, one of several Maine trailer parks where concerns about costs, quality-of-life and ownership arose.

MAINE DEMOCRATS CROWN TROY JACKSON AS PLATNER REPLACEMENT AS FRESH SCRUTINY CLOUDS SENATE RESET

Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Graham Platner and gubernatorial candidate Troy Jackson stand together during a "Fighting Oligarchy" tour stop at the Collins Center for the Arts on the University of Maine campus in Orono on May 24, 2026. (Joe Raedle/Getty Images)

"The other thing that I do hear a lot about, too, is how [landlords] won't do anything for services. And that is completely unfair and not right. And we have to make that change. I feel strongly that if needed, the state should be able to come in [and] take these places over. Some people will say that that's insane," Jackson told the residents in Wells, the town next to the politically-notable Kennebunkport.

"But until the people get the chance to start a co-op or whatever, there should be a way to hold these, so that you don't see private-equity coming in and making the killing on these parks."

PROPERTY OWNER ADVOCACY GROUPS PUSH BACK ON MAMDANI'S 'RENTAL RIPOFF REPORT,' PUBLIC DATABASE OF LANDLORDS

Former State Senator Troy Jackson, a Democrat from Maine and gubernatorial candidate, speaks during a Fighting Oligarchy event with Graham Platner (Sophie Park / Bloomberg via Getty Images)

During his visit, Jackson held up a mason jar of brown water a resident said came from their tap.

Jackson said some residents saw their lot rental fees approach $850, adding he once lived at a mobile home park in Aroostook County and understands their plight.

"I’m going to add my voice to that every damn day," he said. "I just can't imagine owning a home and feeling the threat that you do daily and getting the squeeze and not being able to afford that."

Jackson’s proposal echoes one of the more aggressive elements of Mamdani’s housing agenda: a willingness to use government power to wrest control of troubled properties away from private owners and toward tenants, nonprofits or community stewardship.

MAMDANI RIPPED OVER 'FREAK SHOW' NEWS CONFERENCE WHERE EVICTION WAS DECLARED A FORM OF 'VIOLENCE'

NEW YORK, NEW YORK - JULY 15: Democratic socialist candidate Zohran Mamdani, who won the Democratic primary for mayor of New York City, speaks at an endorsement event from the union DC 37 on July 15, 2025, in New York City. Weeks after Mamdani won the Democratic primary for mayor, various wealthy interest groups have begun to mobilize against the 33-year-old state assemblyman. Mamdani has vowed to freeze rent hikes for a year, make buses free, and increase taxes on wealthy New Yorkers. Former Gov. Andrew Cuomo announced Monday that he will continue his run for New York City mayor after losing to Zohran Mamdani in last month's Democratic primary. (Spencer Platt/Getty Images)

Like Mamdani, Jackson was endorsed by the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) in his prior unsuccessful gubernatorial primary bid earlier this year.

Mamdani’s Block by Block housing plan, released in May, calls for aggressive legal action against negligent landlords and says chronically neglected properties could be transferred to community land trusts, nonprofits or tenants.

BERNIE-BACKED SOCIALIST WHO ALLIED WITH PLATNER COULD SUPPLANT HIM ON BALLOT

"Through the Open-Door program and by supporting community land trusts, we will remove negligent owners and property managers of buildings suffering from chronic neglect or mired in foreclosure and shift ownership to responsible community stewards," Mamdani said in June.

While Mamdani’s more nationally-visible rent-freeze plans are materially different from Jackson’s considerations, they share a common thread: the government should intervene in the housing market when politicians believe pricing or practices are untoward.

MAMDANI’S $22 BILLION HOUSING LUNACY PROPOSAL WILL SOCIALIZE THE SKYLINE

That commonality led to Jackson being lambasted after the fact.

"Another full-on Communist running for office," said Lt. Col. Tony Shaffer [Ret.], a former intelligence officer, posted to X.

"Troy Jackson is ready to violate the rights of Mainers because he feels that they make too much money engaging in free market commerce," Shaffer tweeted. "Spoken here like the true Stalinist he is."

RESURFACED ASSAULT REPORT PUTS DEM SENATE NOMINEE IN GOP CROSSHAIRS: 'GRAHAM PLATNER 2.0'

The Republican National Committee also caught wind of Jackson’s comments, tweeting through their rapid-response arm.

"Troy Jackson wants the government to seize private property from Mainers," they wrote.

Former Maine Senate President Troy Jackson, D-Fort Kent, left; New York Mayor Zohran K. Mamdani, right. (Tom Williams/Getty Images; Kyle Mazza/Getty Images)

Maine law already gives mobile home park residents a limited pathway to take ownership when a park is put up for sale. Under Title 10, Section 9094-A, a group of mobile home owners or a residents’ association has the first option to purchase the park and generally has 60 days after notice of an intended sale to submit an offer.

Fox News Digital reached out to Jackson’s and Collins’ campaigns and Mamdani for comment.

Born and raised in Allentown, Pennsylvania, worked in both the New York and Washington bureaus for Fox News since 2013.

articles.title: Far-right port protests: police told to improve intelligence gathering
articles.excerpt:
Whitehall officials also ask why laws meant to clamp down on the wearing of masks at demonstrations were not used

Police have been told by the government they expect better intelligence gathering aft...
articles.body_text:
Whitehall officials also ask why laws meant to clamp down on the wearing of masks at demonstrations were not used

Police have been told by the government they expect better intelligence gathering after masked far-right groups took to the streets at the weekend, the Guardian has learned, as the Kent force admitted mishandling warnings of potential trouble.

Police in Kent on Saturday and then Portsmouth, Hampshire, on Sunday said they were taken by surprise when hundreds massed to oppose what they say is illegal immigration via small boats.

Both protests are believed by police to have been far-right inspired, with evidence emerging that those behind them were determined to avoid detection.

Claims by Kent police since Saturday that they had no warning fell apart on Tuesday when the force admitted there were warning calls to police on Friday evening which were not acted upon.

Kent police said: “The force had received non-emergency information late on Friday evening that a protest could take place in the town the following day. This information was not fully assessed.”

The government’s view is that police actions once officers were faced by hundreds of men was reasonable.

But there is dismay at how Kent police explained their decision making afterwards, for instance viewing the gathered masked men outside the port of Dover as peaceful protesters, with one source describing it as “fucking crackers”.

On Tuesday evening the prime minister, Andy Burnham, met police chiefs to discuss what had happened and preparedness for any further unrest.

In Dover on Saturday, where hundreds of masked men in black converged undetected, police believe those taking to the streets used walkie-talkies to coordinate their actions.

Police on the ground report the masked men had lawyers’ phone numbers and cited public order case law and were well briefed on how far they could go: “They toed the line perfectly to avoid arrest”, one source said.

In Hampshire police are investigating whether vehicles were deliberately left behind to block access roads.

Police said the Dover gathering passed peacefully, while in Hampshire there were clashes, with the local Police Federation saying anger and violence was directed at officers.

The Guardian understands that part of Hampshire police’s investigation will examine whether the gathering of 200 people was meant to harass or intimidate.

A spokesperson added they are also hunting for those behind the violence, conducting “a thorough review of the body-worn video” to look for offenders.

The protests are believed to have been co-ordinated on closed social media networks and not publicly advertised.

Police are considering whether the threshold for warrants for covert tactics has been met, with one source warning that police were wary of criticism of using “police state tactics” against people portraying themselves as peaceful protesters motivated by a legitimate issue.

The National Police Coordination Centre has intensified its monitoring.

The action in Kent was organised by Daniel Thomas, a long-term associate of the far-right activist Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, known as Tommy Robinson. Thomas, who has established an umbrella grouping called Patriot Platform, was also linked to the blockade in Portsmouth the following day.

Whitehall officials have asked police why tougher laws in place since last year meant to clamp down on the wearing of face masks at protests were not used.

The police view was that at Dover those gathered complied with requests from officers and dispersed after three hours. In Portsmouth, which was more heated, police prioritised a formal dispersal order which they think worked.

Both police and government sources say the “optics”, of masked men in black thronging the streets, looked “intimidating”.

Also on Tuesday it emerged that lifeboat staff who picked up 120 asylum seekers from a large dinghy in the Channel on Sunday were refused entry to two ports shortly before being harangued by right-wing protesters.

Crew on two RNLI vessels were also threatened with legal action if they approached Southampton Port and tried to bring the claimants ashore.

They were forced to take the migrants several miles away to Eastney, where police, firefighters, Border Force and other officials faced protests by up to 200 people, most of whom wore balaclavas and black clothing.

Peter Sparkes, the chief executive of the RNLI, said abuse of its volunteers is “wholly unacceptable in a civilised society”.

He said recent protests had “generated deliberate misinformation and a misunderstanding” about the charity, and condemned threats by “those who would hide behind a balaclava or a keyboard”.

Officials confirmed that a broadcast on an open marine VHF radio said that Southampton Vessel Traffic Service and King’s Harbour Master Portsmouth denied the RNLI permission to enter their ports.

The two RNLI rescue boats from Bembridge and Yarmouth had intercepted a “mega-dinghy” that had left Utah beach near Cherbourg in Normandy.

A spokesperson for Associated British Ports (ABP), which operates the port of Southampton, told the Guardian: “ABP did receive an inquiry about landing recovered migrants at the port of Southampton. We had to decline the inquiry as the port did not have suitable reception facilities available. If there had been a safety of life at sea issue where Southampton was the closest port or if we had received a formal direction from the relevant authority then we would have played a role. Neither was the case in this situation.”

On Tuesday, anti-illegal-migrant protesters attempted to identify RNLI volunteers involved in rescuing those onboard the dinghy. Demonstrators named and shared pictures on X of two people they said were volunteers, claiming they had tracked down an address for one of the men.

Sparkes’s words come after footage posted on social media showed volunteers labelled as “traitors”. In a statement issued on Tuesday, Sparkes said the misinformation led to “some of our volunteers and staff [being] the subject of online and, in the worst cases, physical abuse.

“The RNLI’s people represent the very best in our society. They selflessly give up their time to keep others safe.

“Yet they and their families are being threatened by those who would hide behind a balaclava or a keyboard.

“Their action, in contrast, is wholly unacceptable in a civilised society.

“We will take whatever steps we can to care for and protect our people and their families.”

articles.title: Bombardier defends US manufacturing amid Trump’s aviation sales threat
articles.excerpt:
Bombardier has pushed back against United States President Donald Trump’s threat to block sales of its aircraft if it doesn’t start building planes in the US, saying it already does.

In a statement p...
articles.body_text:
Bombardier has pushed back against United States President Donald Trump’s threat to block sales of its aircraft if it doesn’t start building planes in the US, saying it already does.

In a statement provided to Al Jazeera on Tuesday, the Quebec-based aircraft manufacturer said it employs thousands of workers throughout the US.

“Bombardier aircraft are built with American-made components such as engines, avionics, and many more key systems provided by great American companies,” the aircraft maker said in a statement.

Trump took to Truth Social on Monday, criticising the Canadian company for making 50 percent of its revenue in the US and living off “American Buyers, American Companies, American Airports, and American Service”.

“NO MORE SELLING BOMBARDIER IN THE UNITED STATES! Their products aren’t good enough!” Trump wrote. “If they want our Market, they must build here, and stop treating America like a ‘piggybank’.”

Bombardier, which employs 3,500 people in the US, pointed out that it builds its products in the country, including wings made in the state of Texas and flight control components made in California.

The company also highlighted that it works with suppliers in 47 states, plans to open a new service centre in Fort Wayne, Indiana, and has existing service centres in Arizona, Texas, Kansas, Florida and Connecticut, noting that it spends $2.5bn on suppliers each year.

“Bombardier values its great partnership with American companies and its US employees. Our plan is to continue to invest in our people, our customers, and the communities in which we operate across the country,” the company said.

Senator Jerry Moran, a Republican from Kansas, where Bombardier has its US headquarters, pushed back on the president’s comments on Monday.

“The presence of Bombardier in Wichita supports a local workforce of more than a thousand employees, who contribute their talent and expertise to our nation’s defense and aerospace capabilities,” Moran said on X.

The International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers (IAM) also pushed back on the comments, saying the organisation opposes any attempt to block sales in the US.

The remarks come amid escalating trade tensions between the US and Canada. Early Tuesday, Canada’s retaliatory tariffs took effect, impacting hundreds of US-made products worth $20bn after the White House introduced 50 percent tariffs on Canadian goods.

On Wall Street, Bombardier stock tumbled more than 6.5 percent in midday trading. Meanwhile, its competitors’ stock rose, with Boeing up 0.3 percent and Airbus up 1 percent.

This is not the first spat that Trump has had with the Montreal-area-based airplane maker. In January, Trump accused the company of keeping Gulfstream business jets out of Canadian markets by delaying certification of aircraft.

During Trump’s first term as US president, Boeing accused Bombardier of using government subsidies to sell its passenger jets in the US at artificially low prices. The Commerce Department responded by calculating tariffs of nearly 300 percent on the aircraft. The tariffs, however, never took effect after the US International Trade Commission ruled that Bombardier’s planes had not harmed the American aircraft sector.

Several US airlines also operate Bombardier jets through regional airline partners, including Delta, United, American and Alaska, whose fleets include aircraft operated by carriers such as Endeavor Air and SkyWest.

The White House did not respond to Al Jazeera’s request for comment.

articles.title: Craig Carton blasts Michigan fans for storming field after controversial win: 'They’re a bunch of morons'
articles.excerpt:
Craig Carton's #1 issue with the Michigan game isn't the Big Ten refs, it's the fact that Michigan fans are ridiculously stupid for storming the field following a controversial win over a MAC team

Cr...
articles.body_text:
Craig Carton's #1 issue with the Michigan game isn't the Big Ten refs, it's the fact that Michigan fans are ridiculously stupid for storming the field following a controversial win over a MAC team

Craig Carton scorched Michigan Wolverines fans for celebrating the team’s controversial victory against the Western Michigan Broncos on Saturday night.

There’s no argument that Michigan needed a little bit of luck to get past Western Michigan 13-12. Bryce Underwood received a second Hail Mary opportunity as officials determined that a Western Michigan defended touched his first throw in the final moments with one second left on the clock. Underwood found J.J. Buchanan for the game-winning score.

Is that a real reason to storm the field and act like you beat Ohio State? An emphatic no, says Carton, whose "Craig Carton Show" premieres on OutKick on Tuesday. Carton put it better than I could.

CRAIG CARTON: I'M BRINGING MY 'UNWAVERING, UNAPOLOGETIC' OPINIONS TO OUTKICK

Michigan fans celebrate a narrow win over Western Michigan on Sept. 5, 2026. (Getty Images)

"The thing that bothers me more than the hubris of adding a second to the game and giving Michigan another opportunity to win that game was the fact that there was 110,000 people at Michigan for that game and at the end of the game they stormed the field like they were Western Michigan knocking off a Big Ten team on the road," Carton said. "And it just was a good reminder to me that even though Michigan is thought of as a top educational experience for the kids that take the six years they normally take to graduate, the reality is that they’re a bunch of morons.

"Now, we already know that Michigan is a corrupt athletic program. We know that it’s a dirty athletic program. We know that coaches like to sleep with coeds there. Coaches like to steal signs there. Coaches like to cheat there. But what I didn’t know as a fact until Saturday night is that that 18-27 year olds that call Michigan their undergraduate home are morons. The fact that you would storm the field when barely beating and, let’s be honest, needing the Big Ten to cheat for you to win the game, the fact that you would storm the field when you won by a single point because you were given an extra second of time while 27-point favorites tells me everything I need to know about the type of kid that goes to Michigan."

Michigan fans storm the field after Michigan beat Western Michigan on a Hail Mary touchdown pass with time expired at Michigan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images (Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images)

SUBSCRIBE TO 'THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW' ON YOUTUBE

Remember, it’s not as though Michigan was unranked (they were 16th going into Saturday) and were up against Ohio State or Texas or Alabama or Oregon or even Rutgers for that matter.

The Wolverines were playing Western Michigan that plays in the Mid-American Conference and have been an FBS program since 1962. The Broncos have never beaten an opponent inside the top 20 of the Associated Press poll.

"That’s not a game to be celebrated if you’re a Michigan fan or a Michigan alumni," Carton added. "That’s a game to give you a warning about what’s to come for the rest of this season. Michigan football is dead. Michigan football is an embarrassment. Michigan football pays their quarterback $10 million a year and I would be better.

Nathaniel Owusu-Boateng, No. 12 of the Michigan Wolverines, walks off the field after a 13-12 win over the Western Michigan Broncos at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor, Mich., on Sept. 5, 2026. The Wolverines won on a last-second "Hail Mary" touchdown reception. (Getty Images)

"So, just remember what you saw Saturday night. You saw a Wolverine program that needed cheating and needed secretive clocks to beat a MAC team while favored by 27 points. And the kids there are either so drunk, so high or so stupid that they stormed the field like they had accomplished something. You didn’t accomplish a damn thing but embarrassing yourselves on Saturday night."

Western Michigan has been ranked in the AP poll once ever – that coming in 2016 when they were 13-1 under P.J. Fleck. A victory over a blue blood would have been the biggest win in the program’s history.

The Big Ten and Mid-American Conference both released statements on the clock controversy after the game, reiterating that a Broncos defender touched the ball while out of bounds with one second left.

Michigan fans’ celebration was certainly silly and they will be needled for it until the next cray thing happens.

For now, the team itself has to prepare for noon ET showdown with Oklahoma on Saturday as questions surround Underwood about his status as QB1 for the future.

Bryce Underwood #19 of the Michigan Wolverines celebrates after a 13-12 win over the Western Michigan Broncos at Michigan Stadium on Sept. 5, 2026, in Ann Arbor, Mich. (Getty Images)

Michigan and Oklahoma will battle in Ann Arbor. The game can be seen on FOX.

Ryan Gaydos is a senior editor for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Ukraine’s prosecutor general quits after anti-corruption agents raid his office
articles.excerpt:
Ruslan Kravchenko resigns over allegations some of his officials were engaged in large-scale money laundering

Ukraine’s prosecutor general has resigned after investigators used ladders to raid his of...
articles.body_text:
Ruslan Kravchenko resigns over allegations some of his officials were engaged in large-scale money laundering

Ukraine’s prosecutor general has resigned after investigators used ladders to raid his office in connection with a major corruption scandal that threatens to embarrass Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

Ruslan Kravchenko quit his post on Monday after allegations that some of his officials were involved in large-scale money laundering. They received cash to protect call centres involved in illegal phone scams, it was claimed.

Kravchenko, who denies wrongdoing, left his job after meeting Zelenskyy. Ukraine’s president also spoke to the heads of Nabu and Sapo, the two anti-corruption agencies that have uncovered a sprawling criminal scheme involving government officials.

Zelenskyy described his conversation with Kravchenko as “fairly long” and said: “I’m sure you understand what we discussed.” The prosecutor’s resignation letter will be sent to Ukraine’s parliament, the Verkhovna Rada, he said.

Kravchenko is the latest member of Zelenskyy’s inner circle to be linked to corruption. The allegations involve so-called call centres operating in Ukraine. Employees pose as banks, law enforcement agencies or investment advisers, and persuade victims to transfer funds to accounts or crypto wallets under their control.

Those targeted include Ukrainians, Russians and EU citizens. According to Nabu, a senior official inside the prosecutor general’s office protected the criminal network and helped it to launder its assets.

Each “call centre” paid $7,000 (£5,200) a month in protection money, law enforcement sources told the Ukrainska Pravda newspaper. The bribes ran into millions of dollars, it said, with hundreds of centres believed to employ about 60,000 people across the country.

Nabu investigators raided Kravchenko’s office on Friday. Staff refused to let them in so they used ladders to scale a metal gate. Kravchenko was not at work and had disappeared from his home, which was searched later that evening.

The chief suspect was arrested in the western city of Lviv. Recordings of phone calls published by Nabu suggested he was overseeing repairs at Kravchenko’s home while simultaneously collecting bribes from the fraudulent call centres.

Nabu released images over the weekend of a safe filled with bundles of dollar bills. It said it had uncovered five officials behind the scheme but did not name them. The cash was spent on real estate, jewellery and other valuables, it said, laying out its evidence in a 30-minute video.

Zelenskyy tried to strip Nabu and Sapo of their independence last year, a move he reversed after protests in Kyiv and other cities. There are further claims that the prosecutor’s office subsequently spied on Nabu staff and tried to obstruct their work.

The revelations come at a time when Ukraine is under day-and-night attack from Russian drones and missiles. Three people were killed and 19 injured in overnight strikes on Kyiv that caused huge fires and left smoke hanging over the city.

The onslaught marked the end of a three-day ceasefire in the capital after a visit on Sunday by Donald Trump’s envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. They visited Moscow on Saturday and met Vladimir Putin.

Zelenskyy said the pair had brought some “very good, worthwhile ideas” for ending the war but gave no further details. He said he hoped to meet Trump in the next two weeks. Few expect a breakthrough, with the Kremlin claiming on Tuesday that its forces were close to victory.

While Russia escalated its bombing, Ukrainians were talking about corruption investigations, posting numerous comments on social media, the transparency advocate Olena Tregub said.

“Society is shocked and appalled by government officials who are basically behaving as mafia,” she said. “It’s not even corruption. It’s organised crime, protecting illegal call centres that were scamming people, not only in Ukraine but in Europe.”

She said anti-corruption investigations were different from previous ones because Nabu detectives were “very good technically”.

“They are recording people in their homes, in their offices and over the phone,” she said. “They are outsmarting other law enforcement bodies fighting against them, and are able to tape people who think everything is discreet.”

She said the high-profile raids were “changing the culture in Ukraine” and making society less tolerant of ill-gotten wealth.

Zelenskyy’s former business partner fled the country last year after being implicated in a corruption case featuring the state nuclear energy company. Two ministers were fired. The president’s powerful chief of staff, Andriy Yermak, also later resigned after being questioned. Both deny wrongdoing.

Kravchenko rejected the allegations against him on Sunday, calling them “completely unsubstantiated”. A day later he said he did not want his office “to be used as a tool in political confrontation”.

The deputy chair of parliament’s law enforcement committee, Andriy Osadchuk, said the ​scandal underlined the need to ‌reform the prosecution service ​and called for key posts ​to be filled through open competition. Fighting corruption was also vital to Kyiv’s bid for EU membership, he said.

“It will be very difficult for Ukraine to move forward if we do not change the approach to selecting and appointing the prosecutor general and prosecutors at lower levels,” Osadchuk said.

The head of the Smithsonian Institution announced his retirement Tuesday, stepping down amid an escalating clash with the Trump administration over the leadership and direction of the nation’s museums.

Lonnie Bunch III, who has led the Smithsonian since 2019 and was the founding director of the National Museum of African American History and Culture, said he will leave the post by the end of the year.

"It is with very mixed emotions and heartfelt gratitude that I announce my retirement from the Smithsonian," Bunch said in a press release. "I have spent nearly half of my life working at and being part of the Smithsonian family, and what a privilege it has been. There is no place like the Smithsonian — it has been one of the great loves of my life, and I am extraordinarily proud of what we have accomplished together."

"I leave with pride and sadness, gratitude and joy, and with enormous confidence in the people who will carry this remarkable institution forward," he added.

Families of 9/11 victims and first responders call on Zohran Mamdani to abandon plans to attend the Ground Zero memorial. The 'Outnumbered' panel weighs in.

A coalition of 9/11 family members, first responders, and elected officials gathered on the steps of City Hall on Tuesday to deliver a message to New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani: stay away from this year's Sept. 11 memorial service.

"This mayor is not serving us," said Charles Wolf, who lost his wife on 9/11. "He's serving himself. We are asking respectfully that he not show up, even though there is going to be other politicians there. These are the politicians that helped us push beneficial laws through and literally held our hand during that time. Mayor Mamdani has not shown any of that, none of it. He just wants to be there because he wants to be there. So we are asking him to respect the fact that that trauma is revived during the ceremony. It is a private ceremony. It is not a public ceremony. Mayor Mamdani, please do not come. "

This is a breaking story. Check back here for updates.
