articles.title: Israel to close British consulate in Jerusalem after sanctions announced
articles.excerpt:
Several MPs also banned from Israel after UK steps up condemnation of settlements and announces sweeping sanctions

Israel has ordered the closure of the British consulate in occupied East Jerusalem i...
articles.body_text:
Several MPs also banned from Israel after UK steps up condemnation of settlements and announces sweeping sanctions

Israel has ordered the closure of the British consulate in occupied East Jerusalem in response to sweeping UK sanctions on goods from illegal settlements.

Reacting to Ed Miliband’s description of violent Jewish settler activity on the occupied Palestinian West Bank as “ethnic cleansing” carried out with the tacit backing of the Netanyahu government, Israel’s foreign minister, Gideon Sa’ar, announced retaliatory measures including the closure of the consulate and entry bans on several UK MPs.

It is the latest stage in a furious and escalating row between the countries in which diplomatic relations have hit rock bottom.

The consulate in the Sheikh Jarrah area of the city focuses on Palestinian issues in the occupied territories, including Gaza, the West Bank and Jerusalem. The British embassy in Tel Aviv is where the UK’s ambassador to Israel is based.

While most countries regard East Jerusalem as illegally occupied by Israel since the Six Day War in 1967, Israel says Jerusalem is its undivided capital.

“United Jerusalem is the capital of Israel and is under its full sovereignty,” Sa’ar said. “Any foreign activity in the area must be conducted through accepted and agreed channels and without violating Israel’s sovereignty.”

Sa’ar also announced entry bans on a number of mostly leftwing MPs including the former Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn, the Your Party MP Zarah Sultana, the Labour MPs Diane Abbott, Naz Shah, John McDonnell and Richard Burgon and the Green MPs Hannah Spencer, Carla Denyer, Siân Berry and Ellie Chowns.

The Israeli government added that longstanding British involvement in the training of Palestinian security forces on the West Bank would be terminated. Britain will also be excluded from the US-led Gaza coordination mission, which is based in Israel.

The British sanctions were coordinated with 11 other countries, including France and Canada.

Sa’ar said: “The British move is morally distorted, ​and constitutes blatant interference in the affairs of a sovereign state and its electoral process.”

He added: “Israel has nothing against the British people. We know that we have many friends in Britain. Unfortunately, a hostile Labour government is in office, systematically acting against the state of Israel, and it has left us with no choice but to finally respond to its hostile actions.”

Sa’ar said that he ​had coordinated ‌Israel’s response ​with the prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu. Israel will hold an election in late October.

Israel’s president, Isaac Herzog, called the ban “a grave miscalculation, a decision that will fall on the wrong side of history”.

“In the current context, it would be a gross interference in the democratic elections of a sovereign nation,” he said. “Sanctions are not a solution – dialogue is. I say to all foreign governments: Stop. Step away from the dead-end of sanctions and boycotts, and turn toward constructive dialogue and toward cooperation.”

Settlement building and settlement-related violence have increased under the auspices of far-right Israeli ministers in the Netanyahu government who have said publicly that they aim to “bury” a two state solution through their actions.

Itamar Ben-Gvir, Israel’s hardline public security minister and a settler leader, called on Netanyahu to recognise Argentina’s claim to the Falkland Islands, a British overseas territory in the South Atlantic known in Argentina as Islas Malvinas.

The US ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, a longtime supporter of the settlements, said the British sanctions were “discrimination against the Jewish people”. He said the UK could face “repercussions or retaliations” from the US.

However, in a markedly more muted response, US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, said Washington would ‌not follow Britain, ​France and Canada in blocking ⁠imports from Israeli ​settlements in ​the Palestinian ​territory and did not want to see moves that would destabilise the West Bank.

Israel has been under notice from successive British governments – both Conservative and Labour – for years over the risk of international isolation and potential sanctions related to continuing settlement activity in the occupied territories. These warnings have becomelouder in recent years as violent settler activity has escalated.

The UK’s Labour government previously sanctioned some Israeli settlers and illegal outposts over violence against Palestinians and illegal development in the West Bank.

In a change of Britain’s position, Miliband, the foreign secretary, said on Tuesday that the UK regards Israel’s occupation of the West Bank, and not just the settlements, as illegal.

The tougher stance is likely to be welcomed by many Labour voters and lawmakers, who have urged the government to go further in sanctioning Israel and supporting Palestinians.

Difficulties to establishing an EU-wide approach, coordinated with the UK, had led to countries making individual decisions on a widening sanctions regime that culminated in the joint statement by 12 countries that they were setting in train the process of far harder-hitting sanctions.

articles.title: Robert Saleh and Brian Daboll aim to turn the Tennessee Titans into AFC South contenders
articles.excerpt:
Hutton & Withrow discuss the Tennessee Titans selection of Ohio State wide receiver Carnell Tate.

With defensive-minded head coach Robert Saleh taking over the program and veteran offensive coordinat...
articles.body_text:
Hutton & Withrow discuss the Tennessee Titans selection of Ohio State wide receiver Carnell Tate.

With defensive-minded head coach Robert Saleh taking over the program and veteran offensive coordinator Brian Daboll arriving to shepherd quarterback Cam Ward in his sophomore year, the Tennessee Titans are aiming to prove that its painful baseline rebuild is finally giving way to a competitive new era in the AFC South.

The Titans endured a brutal 2025 campaign, stumbling to a 3–14 finish and landing near the bottom of the league in both scoring offense and scoring defense. Rookie starter Cam Ward showed occasional dynamic flashes under pressure, while Tony Pollard provided steady work out of the backfield with a 1,082-yard rushing season. In fairness, the NFL didn’t do them many favors, giving them a really tough schedule even after a bad year. Ultimately, the lack of success on both sides of the ball led to the mid-season exit of Brian Callahan.

Tennessee Titans coach Robert Saleh speaks with the media before the Titans rookie camp at Vanderbilt Health Football Center in Nashville, Tennessee, on May 1, 2026. (DENNY SIMMONS / THE TENNESSEAN / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images)

To reset the organization, general manager Mike Borgonzi orchestrated a sweeping offseason overhaul.

The headline moves started at the top by hiring former New York Jets head coach Robert Saleh as head coach and bringing in Brian Daboll to call plays. The problem I have is that neither has really proven successful with rebuilding teams – maybe Daboll more than Saleh.

JOSH ALLEN RECALLS HIS ROLE IN BILLS' COACHING SEARCH, DETAILS JOE BRADY’S APPROACH TO NEW ROLE

I do like teams that are intentional about upgrading areas. When you have a lot of areas to upgrade, there are only so many areas you can really make an impact. They signed former New York Giants wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson and tight end Daniel Bellinger, added edge rusher John Franklin-Myers and defensive tackle Solomon Thomas, and bolstered the secondary with cornerbacks Alontae Taylor and Cor'Dale Flott alongside safety Tony Adams.

Tennessee Titans quarterback Cam Ward (1) walks off the field after the team's loss in an NFL football game against the Houston Texans, Sunday, Sept. 28, 2025, in Houston. (AP Photo/David J. Phillip)

They also brought in veteran quarterback Mitchell Trubisky as high-end insurance. In the draft, Tennessee made massive moves by taking wideout Carnell Tate at No. 4 overall and trading back into the first round for pass rusher Keldric Faulk. Major subtractions included letting lingering free agents walk and restructuring line depth to accommodate their fresh rookie class.

The offense features a far more dynamic receiving corps with rookie Carnell Tate on the perimeter alongside Wan'Dale Robinson and Calvin Ridley, providing Ward with the quick-separation weapons he lacked as a rookie. Their line isn’t exactly top-notch, coming in at 29th for the year, but I do think there is potential they are better than they are graded at currently.

HOUSTON TEXANS' 2025 WIN TOTAL SET AT 9.5 AS CJ STROUD FACES QUESTIONS ABOUT OFFENSIVE LINE

Tennessee Titans quarterback Cam Ward throws during the second half an NFL football game against the Indianapolis Colts, Sunday, Oct. 26, 2025, in Indianapolis. (AP Photo/Michael Conroy)

If you plan to bet the over 6.5 wins for Tennessee, I think you attribute it to the improved weapons for Ward, the tough schedule from last season that still saw them get three wins, and the new coaching staff. If you want the under, it is looking at an offensive line that is ranked at 29th, and a defensive line ranked at 17th. The Texans have a great defense, but there are questions on that roster as well. The Colts have a quarterback coming back from an Achilles tear, and the Jaguars lost some key pieces. I have them right at six wins this year, which improves from last year, but I don’t think I can bet one way or another on them.

For more sports betting information and plays, follow David on X/Twitter: @futureprez2024

articles.title: Alex Van Halen calls Sammy Hagar 'a complete idiot' as decades-long feud between bandmates deepens
articles.excerpt:
Sammy Hagar saw his late bandmate Eddie Van Halen in a dream and wrote the song, "Encore, Thank You, Goodnight."

Alex Van Halen has some thoughts about former bandmate Sammy Hagar.

During an intervi...
articles.body_text:
Sammy Hagar saw his late bandmate Eddie Van Halen in a dream and wrote the song, "Encore, Thank You, Goodnight."

Alex Van Halen has some thoughts about former bandmate Sammy Hagar.

During an interview with Brazilian music journalist Marcelo Vieira published earlier this month, Alex ripped into Hagar when asked about his 2011 memoir, "Red: My Uncensored Life in Rock."

"I don't know what he wrote, and I don't wanna know," he said, according to a translation from the original Portuguese interview published by Roadie Crew. "In my opinion, Sammy Hagar is a complete idiot."

SAMMY HAGAR BURIES DECADES-LONG FEUD WITH DAVID LEE ROTH AFTER TOUR DATES ARE AXED

Alex Van Halen called Sammy Hagar a "complete idiot" after decades-long feud.  (Getty Images)

Hagar has since responded to the insult, writing in an Instagram comment over the weekend, "This comment and post is so unnecessary at this time in our lives, but I guess the truth hurts sometimes. Peace already."

The latest jab comes after years of tension between the former bandmates, who have not spoken in more than two decades, according to Hagar.

ENGELBERT HUMPERDINCK MAKES BLUNT ADMISSION ABOUT MYSTERIOUS DECADES-LONG TOM JONES FEUD

A representative for Alex did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

Alex previously rejected an invitation to join Hagar and former Van Halen bassist Michael Anthony for their 2024 "Best of All Worlds" tour, which celebrated Hagar's era with the band.

"I'm not interested," Alex told Billboard at the time. "They're not doing the band justice. They can do what they want to do. That's not my business."

Michael Anthony, Sammy Hagar, Eddie Van Halen and Alex Van Halen pose for a portrait on March 16, 1986. (Paul Natkin/Getty Images)

Alex also largely focused on Van Halen's original lineup with David Lee Roth in his 2024 memoir, "Brothers," while largely omitting Hagar's decade-long run with the band.

GEORGE MICHAEL STRUGGLED WITH 'ETERNAL CONFLICT' OVER FAME, WHAM! BANDMATE ANDREW RIDGELEY SAYS

"What happened after Dave left is not the same band," Alex told Billboard while promoting the book. "I'm not saying it was better or worse or any of that. … But the magic was in the first years, when we didn't know what we were doing, when we were willing to try anything."

Earlier this year, Hagar suggested he would "never play" with Alex again more than 20 years after their last tour together.

"I'm the biggest Pink Floyd fan. I see David Gilmour say, 'I will never play with Roger Waters again,' and I know what he means," the 78-year-old told Classic Rock. "I feel that way about Alex Van Halen. They're negative people."

Hagar seemingly responded to Alex's comments, saying the words were "unnecessary."  (Christopher Polk/Billboard via Getty Images)

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

Hagar, who replaced Roth as lead singer of Van Halen in 1985, remained with the band until 1996. He later reunited with the group in 2004 for a reunion tour.

The singer has suggested that Alex's health problems and inability or unwillingness to continue playing drums may have contributed to the tension. Hagar speculated that Alex could be frustrated that he and Anthony continue to perform Van Halen songs while the drummer is no longer touring.

Hagar told Rolling Stone in April 2025 that he and Alex had not spoken in 21 years.

"I hate to say it, but I dreamt about Alex the other night, man," he told the magazine. "It was crazy. And it was so friggin' real. I was saying, 'What are you pissed off at me about, man? What the f---? Now, just tell me what your problem is. What did I do? Just tell me.'"

Hagar has been open about his feud with Alex Van Halen.  (Matt Winkelmeyer/Getty Images for iHeartRadio)

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Hagar said he thinks Alex is upset with him "because I'm out doing it, and Mike [Anthony] and I are out doing it, and he can't. He's not a singer. He's not a guitar player. He is not really a band leader. And he seems like he doesn't want to play drums or can't play drums anymore, and he can't go write a new record."

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

"Alex wasn't the songwriter in the band," he continued. "He was the drummer. Eddie and I wrote the songs. Dave [Lee Roth] and Eddie wrote the songs, and so we can go out and do them. And I think that really bothers him that Mike and I are still out there doing it. I would feel bad. If I put myself in his shoes, I would feel terrible if I couldn't do it anymore."

Hagar and Alex have not spoken in 21 years.  (Ann Summa/Getty Images)

Alex's criticism also follows Hagar's previous claims that he tried repeatedly to reconnect with his former bandmate, including while assembling the "Best of All Worlds" tour. Hagar said he and Anthony reached out to Alex "a dozen times" before the tour but received no response.

Christina Dugan Ramirez is an entertainment journalist with more than 15 years of experience, including a decade at PEOPLE writing high-profile cover stories, covering Hollywood's biggest events, and interviewing many of the industry's most influential stars before joining Fox News Digital in 2024.

What a week of action to officially start the college football season. We had a mysterious second appear and the sad storming of the field that followed in Week 1 of the season.

Cameras spotted the Ole Miss fan during the third quarter of the Liberty Mutual Music City Kickoff in Nashville as she was showing concern for the Rebels' inability to put the Cardinals away.

Lincoln Kienholz No. 3 of the Louisville Cardinals rushes for a touchdown against the Ole Miss Rebels at Nissan Stadium on Sept. 6, 2026, in Nashville, Tenn. (ISI Photos via Getty Images)

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON’T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

The internet worked its magic and identified her a short time later as Sara Smith. The Ole Miss alum went private on Instagram, but evidently not before she received several DMs.

On Monday night, on TikTok, Smith acknowledged that she was the hot viral Ole Miss fan who became an internet star thanks to a few seconds of camera time and the power of social media.

Mississippi Rebels fans cheer after a touchdown during the Music City Kickoff between Mississippi and Louisville at Nissan Stadium in Nashville, Tenn., on Sept. 6, 2026. (Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

articles.title: Adidas apologizes after ad featuring former Israeli soldier who lost leg draws boycott calls
articles.excerpt: Nike prepares to leave the S&P 100 index on September 21 after hitting its weakest valuation in 12 years on Friday. FOX Business contributor Josh Schaefer details the company's direct-to-consumer stru...
articles.body_text:
Nike prepares to leave the S&P 100 index on September 21 after hitting its weakest valuation in 12 years on Friday. FOX Business contributor Josh Schaefer details the company's direct-to-consumer struggles and fierce brand competition. Schafer highlights that Nike lost 76% of its value over five years, underperforming the broader market as consumer behaviors shift.

Adidas has issued an apology for any "offense" the company caused with its recent advertisement that featured an Israel Defense Forces veteran who lost a leg while serving.

"We recognize that an image used in a recent local activation by the local team has raised concerns and strong reactions. It was never our intent to cause offense and we apologize for anyone affected," the company said in a statement, according to The Times of Israel.

"We acknowledge the concerns that have been raised and are taking the feedback seriously."

An Adidas logo is seen on the street in Warsaw, Poland, on August 15, 2026. (Photo by Klaudia Radecka/NurPhoto via Getty Images) (Klaudia Radecka/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

WNBA STAR SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM'S PLAYER EXCLUSIVE ADIDAS SHOE SELLS OUT IN LESS THAN AN HOUR ONLINE

The initiative, which was limited to Adidas outlets in Israel, included posters and videos featuring 10 disabled athletes. The campaign was focused on the company's single shoe service, showcasing athletes who require just one shoe due to amputations or accidents.

Veteran Shalev Biton, who lost in May 2021 during the conflict in Gaza, was featured in the advertisement. The Hebrew-language video did not mention Biton's army service or an explanation of how he lost his leg.

Pedestrians walk past an Adidas store at the Taikoo Li Sanlitun shopping complex on August 22, 2026, in Beijing, China. China is seeking to bolster domestic demand and sustain economic growth amid continued pressure from a prolonged property downturn, cautious consumer spending and global trade uncertainties. (Photo by Cheng Xin/Getty Images) (Cheng Xin/Getty Images)

OUTKICK IS NOW ON THE FOX APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

Criticism falsely claimed that Biton was involved in the recent fighting in Gaza, with anti-Israel activists accusing him of participating in "genocide." In reality, his accident occurred more than five years ago when an anti-tank missile fired from inside Gaza hit the military vehicle he was in on the Israeli side of the border. Fellow soldier Staff Sgt. Omer Tabib was killed during the action.

"Across the Middle East, Adidas has a long-standing commitment to the communities we serve, working alongside athletes, teams and sporting communities throughout the region as well as supporting people and communities in need through product donations," Adidas' statement continued.

"We will continue to listen, learn and work to ensure that our actions reflect the inclusive values we stand for."

of Adidas, of the German sports equipment manufacturer, in Strasbourg, eastern France, on August 24, 2024. (Photo by Abdesslam MIRDASS / AFP) (Photo by ABDESSLAM MIRDASS/AFP via Getty Images) (ABDESSLAM MIRDASS/AFP via Getty Images)

Biton, who returned to running with a prosthetic limb, took to social media amid the intense wave of backlash he received online following the advertisement.

"Been hit by an absolutely insane wave of hatred and reports from all over the world," Biton wrote to his Instagram followers, per The Jerusalem Post. "Some of the biggest pro-Palestinian pages in the world, with millions of followers and millions of likes and shares, have been posting about me again and again, and the abuse and reports just don’t stop," he continued.

The recent war in Gaza began in October 2023.

articles.title: SEC accuses LSU of letting Lane Kiffin run wild as expulsion vote coming Thursday in explosive court filing
articles.excerpt:
Will LSU be able to start former NFL players??

The SEC filed an amended complaint Tuesday morning in an Alabama federal court, indicating that the conference is seriously considering drastic action a...
articles.body_text:
Will LSU be able to start former NFL players??

The SEC filed an amended complaint Tuesday morning in an Alabama federal court, indicating that the conference is seriously considering drastic action against LSU.

After what unfolded last week in a Louisiana district court, it has become clear that the fight launched by LSU over the potential rostering of athletes with NFL experience has not gone over well with officials inside SEC headquarters.

Last Thursday, while SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey took the stand in a Baton Rouge courtroom, the conference filed a federal lawsuit against LSU, head coach Lane Kiffin and athletic department staffers. The lawsuit argued that the school was preventing SEC officials from exercising their First Amendment rights to govern the conference.

LSU HOLDS OFF ON ADDING PLAYERS WITH NFL TIES AS SEC LAWSUIT LOOMS OVER PROGRAM, LANE KIFFIN

LSU Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin talks with SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey during SEC Media Day 2026 at the JW Marriott Water Street on July 23, 2026, in Tampa, Fla. (University Images via Getty Images)

Sankey testified for more than three hours, a hearing OutKick attended, and the gamesmanship quickly disappeared. Behind the scenes, the SEC was preparing to take action against LSU over a fiasco that had placed the conference and its leadership at the center of what was viewed as an embarrassing situation in Birmingham.

"The SEC does not bring this action to declare any student-athlete ineligible or to prevent any student-athlete from participating in any athletic competition. This action is directed solely at the state actors who have violated, continue to violate, and threaten to further violate the SEC’s rights under the First Amendment," the complaint noted.

LSU MIGHT HAVE TO SUE THE SEC IF THIS LEGAL WAR IS EXPEDITED, WHILE DABO SWINNEY IS STAYING IN HIS 'LANE'

The fight is now moving beyond the courtroom.

On Thursday, SEC officials will hold a special meeting to determine whether LSU could face expulsion from the conference. The meeting centers on concerns that school officials have lost control of Kiffin and the football program.

In the filing, SEC presidents and chancellors made it clear during a Sept. 4 meeting that they feel as though LSU has let Lane Kiffin run the football program however he wants, without guidance from the athletic department.

"Expressed great concern that Defendants Rousse and Ausberry have no meaningful control over Defendant Kiffin or the football program at LSU...The consensus at the September 4 meeting was and continues to be that LSU’s demonstrated lack of institutional control at the University level—including complete lack of control over Defendant Kiffin’s actions."

Simply put, the SEC feels as though the comments made by Kiffin over the past few weeks regarding this matter go against conference rules, and they feel as though the LSU athletic department has allowed Kiffin to run the football program without pressure from his own bosses.

That's up to the member institutions, though the likelihood of the SEC expelling LSU from the conference feels pretty slim in the grand scheme of things.

Head coach Lane Kiffin of the LSU Tigers in action during fall practice at Tiger Stadium on August 29, 2026 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. (Photo by Gus Stark/LSU/University Images via Getty Images) (Gus Stark/LSU/University Images via Getty Images)

But, in their updated filing on Tuesday, the SEC made it clear that they have the power to expel LSU from the conference, if enough votes are cast in favor of the move.

"Membership of a member may be terminated involuntarily at a meeting of the Chief Executive Officers. A vote of at least two-thirds of all the Chief Executive Officers is required to terminate membership. Any motion to terminate membership shall specify the effective date of the proposed termination," the complaint notes.

Right now, we are witnessing a fight between one of the biggest schools in the conference, and SEC members who are tired of being made fools of by Kiffin.

LSU'S LANE KIFFIN ADMITS HE LET TIGER STADIUM WEATHER DELAY DRAG ON IN ORDER TO HURT CLEMSON

And, when Sankey took the stand last week inside a Baton Rouge courthouse, the stakes were raised in this matter to the point where the SEC has now made it clear that they are not going to just brush this under the table because LSU decided not to roster players like Dae'Quan Wright this past weekend.

This has obviously ruffled plenty of feathers, and Kiffin's comments during the Clemson game this past weekend regarding how much worse the outcome could have been if LSU had been able to roster pro players were seen as the school having zero control over its head coach.

LSU’S LANE KIFFIN FIRES BACK AT NFL RETURNEE BACKLASH: BLAME THE NCAA, NOT US FOR RECRUITING PRO ATHLETES

"Defendant Kiffin’s statements and position, along with the numerous other statements and actions by Defendants alleged herein, stand in sharp contrast to the silence by the President and Athletic Director of LSU after Defendant Rousse voted for the Policy Statement on August 25, 2026," the SEC noted in its amended complaint.

"And they confirm the lack of institutional control over the athletics program at LSU that is required by Article 6 of the SEC Constitution and by the remaining provisions of the Constitution and Bylaws referenced above."

Not only is the SEC under the impression that LSU is allowing Lane Kiffin to run his football program without guidance from school officials, they see this as a slap in the face to the rules enacted regarding pro-athletes coming back to college.

"In light of the recalcitrance, lack of institutional control, and serious harm caused by the statements and conduct of LSU, the 15 SEC CEOs (other than LSU) have informally told the Commissioner (and President Plowman has directed the Commissioner) to issue a notice of the Special Meeting to be conducted on September 10, 2026, to consider the termination of LSU’s membership in the SEC, whether LSU renounces its intention to roster and play professional players on its football team, or not."

LSU Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin looks on against Clemson during the first half at Tiger Stadium in Baton Rouge, La., on Sept. 5, 2026. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect)

The SEC is obviously past the point of frustration with Lane Kiffin, and now we're about to find out how serious they are regarding penalties against the school in which they feel has embarrassed them enough.

Just when you thought the college football season would provide us an opportunity to talk about other things taking place outside a courtroom, the SEC decided to drop a public hammer on Tuesday.

Will they actually do it? Probably not, but they clearly want to embarrass LSU in the process.

Trey Wallace is the Sr. College Sports Reporter for OutKick.

articles.title: FIBA Women's World Cup players' hotel evacuated after fire breaks out ahead of high-stakes final stage
articles.excerpt: OutKick Reporter Jackson Thompson joins Riley Gaines to break down what he’s seeing inside the WNBA’s biggest cultural moment. Riley and Jackson discuss Caitlin Clark, Sophie Cunningham, the Indiana F...
articles.body_text:
OutKick Reporter Jackson Thompson joins Riley Gaines to break down what he’s seeing inside the WNBA’s biggest cultural moment. Riley and Jackson discuss Caitlin Clark, Sophie Cunningham, the Indiana Fever, WNBA fan energy, league growth, media gatekeeping, and whether the league is prepared for its expanding audience. They also discuss the ongoing debate over men in women’s sports, questions around WNBA eligibility policies, Enes Kanter Freedom, Royce White, San Jose State volleyball, and how sports media has covered female athletes speaking out. Plus, Jackson shares what he’s watching next as the WNBA postseason approaches and Team USA women’s basketball prepares for international competition.

Women’s Basketball World Cup teams were forced to evacuate their Berlin hotel early Tuesday morning for the second time in three days, after a fire started in a neighboring parking facility.

FIBA said the alarm went off at 9:06 a.m. local time. The teams followed standard safety procedures and assembled outside before returning to their rooms at 9:27 a.m.

"Following a thorough inspection, it was confirmed that the alarm was activated due to the start of a fire in the garbage room located in the underground basement of a neighbouring parking facility," FIBA said in a statement.

A basketball goal stands in front of a logo for the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup 2026 outside the Max Schmelling Hall, one of two venues hosting the competition in Berlin on Sept. 3, 2026. The competition takes place from Sept. 4 to 13, 2026. (AFP via Getty Images)

"The Police are currently investigating the exact circumstances surrounding the incident."

The U.S. team was not affected because the Americans are staying at a different hotel from the rest of the tournament field.

Napheesa Collier, Kahleah Copper, Breanna Stewart and Chelsea Gray of the USA Women's National Team look on during a game against China at the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup 2026 on Sept. 4, 2026, at Max-Schmeling-Halle in Berlin, Germany. (NBAE)

WNBA STAR WILL MISS PLAYING IN FIBA WORLD CUP AFTER HER PASSPORT GOES MISSING IN THE MAIL

The incident came two days after an alarm forced players and coaches out of the same hotel at approximately 2 a.m. Sunday. That evacuation lasted about an hour and disrupted the sleep of teams scheduled to play later that day.

FIBA said Tuesday that the first alarm "was due to steam in the kitchen during its cleaning." Australia coach Sandy Brondello had previously said she was told someone activated an emergency alarm in an elevator, according to The Associated Press.

THE PREDOMINANT BASKETBALL DYNASTY ON EARTH IS AT STAKE AS AMERICA'S EYES TURN TO CAITLIN CLARK'S ROLE

The Uber Arena in Berlin on Nov. 9, 2024. (dpa/picture alliance via Getty Images)

Tuesday’s evacuation occurred on the opening day of the knockout stage. Hungary and Japan were scheduled to play the first qualification game, followed by host Germany against South Korea. The winners will advance to face the U.S. and Belgium, respectively, in Thursday’s quarterfinals.

FIBA did not report any injuries or changes to the tournament schedule.

"The safety of all participants remains FIBA’s priority and we are taking all measures to make sure that the teams are put in the best possible conditions to compete," the organization said.

Jackson Thompson is a sports reporter for Fox News Digital covering critical political and cultural issues in sports, with an investigative lens. Jackson's reporting has been cited in federal government actions related to the enforcement of Title IX, and in legacy media outlets including The New York Times, The Los Angeles Times, The Philadelphia Inquirer, The Associated Press and ESPN.com.

articles.body_text:
The Boston Red Sox are one win away from tying the longest winning streak in franchise history at 15 games, a record set in 1946.

For whatever reason, the betting gods have rained down their fury on me over the past few days. I have been losing virtually every bet that I have placed. College football started, and I had the worst weekend I've ever had betting on the sport. I bet big on the Blue Jays yesterday and Dylan Cease let me down. Not exactly what I am looking for as a sports betting analyst. As always, the good news is that we get betting options daily, and we can get some of that money back on this one between the Angels and Red Sox.

The Los Angeles Angels are in the midst of yet another lost season. They will almost certainly finish as the worst team in their division, and potentially the worst team in baseball. Another 100-loss season is on the horizon unless they can win seven of their final 18 games. Considering they are winning only 38% of their games, it seems a bit unlikely that they will get the seven wins needed to avoid the 100-loss fate. The only good news is that this team is being sold, and perhaps new ownership will turn this franchise around.

Los Angeles Angels third baseman Vaughn Grissom runs after hitting an RBI single against the St. Louis Cardinals during the first inning at Angel Stadium in Anaheim, Calif., on July 21, 2026. (Gary A. Vasquez/Imagn Images)

Detmers has been worse on the road this season, but his numbers aren't terrible. His road ERA is 3.80, compared with 3.21 at home. He has been fantastic since the start of August, going 37 innings and allowing just six earned runs. One of his worst starts of the season came against Boston, where he allowed five earned runs over five innings.

The Boston Red Sox avoided a disaster season by becoming one of the hottest teams in baseball history. They have been extremely streaky over the past couple of months, winning a ton, then losing a few in a row. They've won their past five games, including the series opener yesterday. However, even this win streak saw them lose six of their previous eight games before starting this streak. And before that, they won five games in a row again. The team is currently 15 games above .500 and owners of the second Wild Card spot.

Caleb Durbin #5 of the Boston Red Sox celebrates with Jarren Duran #16 and Ceddanne Rafaela #3 after hitting a walk-off RBI single against the Chicago White Sox in the 13th inning at Fenway Park on Aug. 6, 2026, in Boston, Mass. (Getty Images)

Looking to extend this winning streak is tonight's starter, Patrick Sandoval. It is hard to bet against the Red Sox in any game recently because of how well they've played. For the year, Sandoval is 1-4 with a 4.41 ERA and a 1.73 WHIP. He has only made 10 starts for Boston this year, and is allowing an earned run basically every other inning that he pitches. He hasn't been great lately, with 17 earned runs allowed over his last 30 innings of work. He didn't face the Angels this season, but their team is hitting just 4-for-17 against him in their careers.

Los Angeles Angels pitcher Reid Detmers throws against the New York Yankees at Angel Stadium in Anaheim, Calif., on Sept. 2, 2026. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect)

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

The Angels are terrible on the road, though, at just 24-46. I'm going to take the Angels tonight through five innings behind Detmers. I don't know that they can pull off the full game, but I do think their starting pitching advantage will give them the edge in this game. Give me the Angels through five innings on the moneyline.

articles.title: Iran-backed attacks threaten a second major oil chokepoint as new risk emerges for US consumers
articles.excerpt: Houthi rebels attack Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea, causing oil prices to surge. This logistical nightmare prompts strong warnings from President Donald Trump to Iran, holding them responsible for ...
articles.body_text:
Houthi rebels attack Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea, causing oil prices to surge. This logistical nightmare prompts strong warnings from President Donald Trump to Iran, holding them responsible for the Houthi actions.

Iran-backed Houthi rebels struck Saudi Arabia with dozens of ballistic missiles and drones Tuesday, hitting multiple energy targets, including the facilities of the world's largest oil company.

The attacks on Aramco, the state-owned national oil company of Saudi Arabia that produces 10 million barrels of oil per day, threaten to tighten pressure on a second critical oil route as the Middle East war continues to restrict shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

Aramco notably supplies roughly 10% of the world's total oil demand. And attacks on its facilities raise the risk of higher oil, shipping and transportation costs that could hit U.S. consumers in coming months — just in time for the 2026 midterm elections.

IRAN CALLS ON HOUTHIS TO PREPARE TO CUT OFF RED SEA GATEWAY — CAN THE TERROR GROUP DO IT?

Houthi supporters chant slogans during an anti-U.S. and anti-Israel rally in Sanaa, Yemen, Monday, March 17, 2025. (AP Photo/Osamah Abdulrahman)

The attacks hit the southern Saudi Arabian cities of Jazan, Najran, Abha and Khamis Mushait, wounding 73 people and sparking fires at energy facilities and utilities that temporarily forced some operations to stop, according to Saudi officials. The Jazan site includes a refinery capable of processing roughly 400,000 barrels of crude per day, according to the Associated Press.

Tuesday's strikes land at a particularly vulnerable moment for global energy markets. With oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz sharply reduced, Saudi Arabia has redirected more crude toward the Red Sea — increasing the importance of the Bab el-Mandeb, where the Houthis have already threatened and attacked Saudi-linked shipping.

The Energy Information Administration estimates that just 4.9 million barrels of oil and petroleum liquids moved through Hormuz per day in the second quarter of 2026, down from 21.6 million barrels per day before the conflict. Before the conflict 20% of the world's oil moved through the consequential waterway.

Traffic through the Bab el-Mandeb, meanwhile, averaged 8.1 million barrels per day during the quarter as Saudi Arabia redirected more crude to bypass Hormuz amid ongoing conflict.

That creates a potentially costly vulnerability: renewed Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure or commercial vessels could put pressure on two crucial oil routes at once, raising the risk of higher crude, shipping and transportation costs that could eventually reach U.S. consumers.

Brent crude was trading near $99 per barrel Tuesday.

Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree claimed responsibility for Tuesday’s strikes, saying the group had used "dozens of ballistic missiles and drones" against Aramco facilities, the Jazan industrial zone and a Saudi air base, according to Xinhua.

RUBIO ACCUSES IRAN OF FLYING IRGC PERSONNEL INTO YEMEN AS HOUTHI THREAT ESCALATES

The Houthis said the operation was retaliation for Saudi airstrikes in Yemen and threatened "stronger and wider strikes" if Riyadh’s military campaign continues.

The escalation also comes with a warning already issued by President Donald Trump.

A satellite imagery shows Bab el Mandeb Strait, a key shipping waterway and the gateway to the Red Sea, as Iran threatens using Yemen's Houthi allies to shut the Bab el-Mandeb gateway to the Red Sea, in this handout picture dated July 12, 2026. (Nasa Worldview/Handout via Reuters)

After the Houthis struck two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea in July, Trump said the U.S. would hold Iran responsible if the group attacked ships again and threatened "major military punishment" against both Tehran and the Houthis.

"If they do this again, the U.S. will hold Iran responsible, in that the Houthis are a Surrogate and/or Proxy of Iran, and major military punishment will be inflicted upon Iran and, of course, the Houthis, themselves," Trump wrote on Truth Social at the time.

The warning followed the Houthis’ announcement of a maritime blockade targeting Saudi Arabia and attacks on Saudi tankers in the Red Sea. The escalation sent Brent crude above $100 per barrel amid fears that disruption could spread from the Strait of Hormuz to the Bab el-Mandeb.

The latest strikes targeted Saudi territory and energy infrastructure rather than ships, leaving unclear whether the White House considers them to cross the line Trump drew in July. It creates a new test for the administration as Houthi attacks increasingly intersect with the wider conflict over Iran and regional energy supplies.

The Trump administration has previously authorized U.S. strikes against Houthi weapons and infrastructure in Yemen in response to attacks and threats against American forces and shipping. A White House report says Trump directed those actions to defend U.S. forces and protect American national-security interests.

The U.S. Maritime Administration also maintains an active advisory warning that the Houthis continue to pose a threat to commercial vessels in the southern Red Sea, the Bab el-Mandeb and the Gulf of Aden.

From November 2023 through October 2025, the Houthis carried out more than 100 attacks on commercial vessels affecting more than 60 nations, according to the MARAD advisory. The attacks forced major shipping companies to avoid the Red Sea and reroute vessels around the Cape of Good Hope, adding time to voyages and increasing fuel, freight and insurance costs.

The Houthis renewed that threat in July when they targeted Saudi oil tankers and threatened a blockade of Saudi shipping through the Red Sea.

Saudi Arabia’s increased reliance on the route makes another sustained disruption potentially more consequential. The EIA says alternate routes used to bypass disrupted waterways are longer, more expensive and limited in capacity.

Oil tankers and cargo ships line up in the Strait of Hormuz as seen from Khor Fakkan, United Arab Emirates, Wednesday, March 11, 2026. (Altaf Qadri/AP Photo)

The latest strikes threaten to revive pressure on the Red Sea route just as the Iran conflict has made the Persian Gulf route more difficult to use. The Houthis may lack the capability to permanently close the Bab el-Mandeb, but repeated missile, drone or tanker attacks could still reduce traffic through the waterway if shipping companies determine the risks are too high.

Saudi Arabia condemned Tuesday’s strikes on civilian and economic assets and vowed to defend its territory. The Saudi-led coalition described the attacks as a "dangerous escalation" and said it would take measures to deter further attacks.

The immediate economic impact will depend on how quickly Saudi Arabia restores affected operations and whether commercial shipping continues moving through the Bab el-Mandeb.

The next test could be whether the Houthis again target tankers or other commercial vessels. Another attack could put greater pressure on a waterway carrying an increased share of Middle Eastern oil — while also testing Trump’s warning that renewed Houthi attacks on shipping would bring U.S. retaliation against both the group and Iran.

articles.title: New Hampshire and Rhode Island to vote in state primaries - US politics live
articles.excerpt:
Voters will choose candidates across full slate of federal, state and local offices over next two days

Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.

New Hampshire and Rhode Island primary voters w...
articles.body_text:
Voters will choose candidates across full slate of federal, state and local offices over next two days

Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.

New Hampshire and Rhode Island primary voters will choose candidates across a full slate of federal, state and local offices over the next two days.

In New Hampshire, US senator Jeanne Shaheen’s decision to not seek reelection created a cascade of competitive races, AP reported. Two of the eight Republicans hoping to replace the three-term Democrat are former US senators she previously defeated: John E. Sununu and Scott Brown.

The five-way race for the Democratic nomination includes US representative Chris Pappas, whose departure from his 1st congressional district seat in turn attracted a crowd of candidates.

Shaheen’s daughter, Stefany Shaheen, is among those seeking the Democratic nomination for Pappas’ seat, along with former candidate Maura Sullivan. Several other candidates in top races also are making repeat appearances.

Meanwhile, in Rhode Island, governor Dan McKee faces a tough Democratic primary challenge tomorrow in his bid for a second full term. Voters will also choose nominees for a full slate of federal, state and local offices.

McKee was elected governor by a wide margin in 2022 after first assuming the role in March 2021 when then-governor Gina Raimondo stepped down to become US commerce secretary. He now is at risk of becoming the nation’s first elected governor since 2014 to lose renomination and the first in Rhode Island since 1994.

His challenger is Helena Buonanno Foulkes, a former longtime executive with Rhode Island-based CVS. She placed a close second behind McKee in the five-way 2022 Democratic primary. She is the niece of former Democratic senator Chris Dodd of Connecticut.

President Donald Trump said on Monday that ⁠Canadian private jet maker Bombardier would ⁠no longer be allowed ​to sell its planes in the United States unless it started manufacturing in the country. “NO MORE SELLING BOMBARDIER IN THE UNITED STATES! Their products aren’t good enough!” Trump said in a post on Truth Social. “If ⁠they want our Market, they must build here, and stop treating America like a ’piggybank’.”

New York mayor Zohran Mamdani is set to come face-to-face with Rudy Giuliani at the main September 11 memorial service, just days after the former mayor – who led the city at the time of the 2001 terrorist attacks – disparaged his Muslim religion and said he should skip the ceremony. In an interview with right-leaning Newsmax at the weekend, Giuliani said: “Having lost friends there and being very close to many of the families, it offends me that he’s coming.”

A cluster of advocacy groups that boast veteran lawyers, voting experts and ex-judges have expanded legal challenges to Donald Trump’s authoritarian executive orders on voting and other presidential actions they see as a “war” on the rule of law in the US. Heavy legal opposition to Trump’s two executive orders on elections to curb voting rights and supplant the authority of states on election matters has come from the Democracy Defenders Fund, the Campaign Legal Center, the American Civil Liberties Union and kindred groups.

The US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) recently released a report linking “gender ideology” to leftwing authoritarianism and political violence – a study scientists say was poorly conducted and “nakedly political”, likely leading to greater politicization of science and health. It follows attempts by the administration to limit access to gender-affirming care – including, on Friday, an agreement reached between the Department of Justice and a New York hospital to no longer offer pediatric gender-affirming care.

Democrats are starting to hit back against Donald Trump for his recent social media post suggesting that the state of New Mexico should be changed to “New America”.

The state’s senior senator, Martin Heinrich, shot back on X, blasting the president’s recent efforts to rename bodies of water via executive order.

“Three things I will always call by their actual names,” Heinrich wrote. “The Gulf of Mexico, Lake Ontario, New Mexico.”

Similarly, Melanie Stansbury, one New Mexico’s Democratic US House representatives, was resolute. “WE ARE NOT CHANGING OUR NAME!” she said in a video, standing on the banks of the Rio Grande, which runs through the state. “New Mexico is New Mexico. We are fiercely proud of our name, our people, and our places, including this river.”

Donald Trump is in Washington today. We’ll hear from the president at 10.35am ET, when he hosts an event on the Ellipse honoring first responders at the 9/11 terrorist attacks, ahead of the 25th anniversary commemoration this week.

Trump is set to unveil a 21-foot steel beam that has been recovered from the World Trade Center that will be on display as part of a “Steel Across America” tour.

However, as we noted last week, the president is reportedly not going to be in New York for the anniversary event at Ground Zero, and instead will deliver remarks at the Pentagon. It has long been policy that there are no speeches from the president at the site of the attacks, in order to keep any memorials apolitical.

Trump will spend the rest of the day in closed-door meetings. At 1pm ET he’s set to sign executive orders, and we’ll let you know if that opens up to the press.

President Donald Trump spent Labor Day posting memes on social media in support ⁠of changing the ⁠name ​of the state of New Mexico to ‘New America’ as tense trade negotiations ⁠with Mexico ramp up.

Trump posted several maps of the US that relabelled the land ⁠area of New Mexico as New America ​on Monday.

The president ‌on Sunday said ‌he had received suggestions to change the name ‌of the state and that he liked the idea. “So much more prestigious and beautiful for the people of that potentially incredible State. Wow, I Love It!!!“

Trump’s posts follow his decision ‌to change the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America last month, after ​trade negotiations with Canada failed to produce a deal.

The US federal government, however, has no authority to change the name of a state. New Mexico ⁠is currently governed by Michelle Lujan Grisham, a Democrat. ​She ​has been in ​the job since 1 January, 2019, ​and was reelected ‌in 2022.

The ​governor said ​in a post on X that “New Mexico’s name isn’t up for debate - it’s been ours since before the United States existed.”

The Trump administration is seeking greater US access to Venezuela’s minerals, including gold, as it expands its push to gain control and influence over the South American country’s vast natural resources beyond oil, according to three sources familiar with the discussions.

The effort could open the Venezuelan mining sector to US investment and give ⁠U.S. companies access to not only oil, ⁠but supplies of minerals crucial for national security, ​the sources said on condition of anonymity.

It also would expand president Donald Trump’s push to more closely align Venezuela’s resources with Washington’s strategic and economic interests in the wake of the US military’s ouster of Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro in a raid in January.

New York mayor Zohran Mamdani is set to come face-to-face with Rudy Giuliani at the main September 11 memorial service, just days after the former mayor – who led the city at the time of the 2001 terrorist attacks – disparaged his Muslim religion and said he should skip the ceremony.

In an interview with right-leaning Newsmax at the weekend, Giuliani said: “Having lost friends there and being very close to many of the families, it offends me that he’s coming.”

Mamdani confirmed on Monday, while attending a breakfast celebrating New York’s J’ouvert and West Indian Day Parade celebrations in Brooklyn, that he would attend the main ceremony and multiple 9/11 events on Friday, to stand with the families of those who died and first responders – as he did last year before taking office.

“I’m proud to be the mayor of this city. I love this city. I love this country,” he said. “What I want this week to be a focus on is on the families whose loved ones were stolen from them 25 years ago in the horrific act of terror of September 11, and a focus also on the first responders who did everything they could.”

The mayor and his office have declined to respond to Giuliani’s remarks.

Giuliani, the former mayor and a close ally of Donald Trump, has said he will also attend this year’s ceremony to mark the attacks by terrorists representing al-Qaida, who flew hijacked passenger planes into the twin towers of the World Trade Center in lower Manhattan on September 11 2001.

Reflecting pools with waterfalls constructed on the footprints of the towers and a 9/11 museum now mark the site that was dubbed Ground Zero in the aftermath of the attacks, and where each year the names of the almost 3,000 people who died are read out by survivors and loved ones, in a solemn ceremony attended by national and local leaders.

In the interview with Newsmax, Giuliani was asked if Mamdani should skip the ceremony. “Well, there’s no question he should,” he said.

Iceland summoned the US ambassador on Monday after president Donald Trump posted an image on ⁠social media showing the island and other countries covered by the American flag, local broadcaster RUV said.

The map showed the ⁠United States, Canada, ⁠Greenland, Iceland, Mexico, ​Central America and the Caribbean covered by the US flag, with the entire landmass labelled ‘United States of America’.

Trump posted ⁠the image on his Truth Social platform without explanation.

Iceland’s foreign minister, Thorgerdur Gunnarsdottir, called in Billy Long, the US ambassador to Iceland, ⁠who only formally took up the post last month, RUV reported.

“The position was ​clearly expressed that the post ‌was completely inappropriate,” the foreign ‌ministry told RUV.
