articles.title: What does Mondlane’s trial mean for Mozambique?
articles.excerpt: Maputo, Mozambique – Nearly two years after a disputed presidential election was followed by months of protests in Mozambique, opposition politician Venancio Mondlane is preparing to face trial before...
articles.body_text:
Maputo, Mozambique – Nearly two years after a disputed presidential election was followed by months of protests in Mozambique, opposition politician Venancio Mondlane is preparing to face trial before the country’s Supreme Court.

Mondlane was notified by the court on August 25, 2026, that he would stand trial over five charges linked to the protests that followed the October 2024 election. He is not under arrest and has not yet stood trial. Mondlane said he expected proceedings to begin within two or three months, although no exact date had been announced.

The charges are public advocacy of crime, incitement to collective disobedience, public instigation to a crime, instigation to terrorism and incitement to terrorism. Prosecutors brought the charges in July 2025 over Mondlane’s alleged role in the post-election unrest. He denies the accusations.

Salomão Moyana, a veteran Mozambican journalist and political commentator, told Al Jazeera:

“This trial is politically untimely, given the country’s current political situation. But at the same time, it is legally timely for Venancio himself, because it gives him an opportunity to finally put these pending cases behind him.”

“He is not being accused by the court; he is being accused by the Public Prosecutor’s Office, by the Attorney General’s Office. The court is there to adjudicate.”

Mondlane was an independent presidential candidate backed by the Podemos party in the October 2024 election. He finished second to Daniel Chapo, the candidate of the ruling Mozambique Liberation Front (Frelimo).

The Constitutional Council confirmed Chapo as the winner with 65.17 percent of the vote. Mondlane received 24.19 percent. Mondlane rejected the result and said he had won.

The disputed result was followed by months of demonstrations. More than 300 people were killed in the post-election unrest, according to Reuters.

Prosecutors accuse Mondlane of contributing to the unrest through calls for protests and other forms of resistance, including messages posted on social media. He has rejected the allegations.

Andre Mulungo, an activist with the Centre for Democracy and Development (CDD), told Al Jazeera:

“The trial of Venancio Mondlane reflects a broader pattern of the judicialisation of politics in Mozambique. A crisis that is essentially political, marked by disputes over the election results and a lack of trust in electoral processes, cannot be resolved in the courts. Political problems require political solutions.”

Mondlane left Mozambique in October 2024 and went into self-imposed exile after the disputed election.

He said he feared for his life after Elvino Dias, his lawyer and adviser, and Podemos spokesperson Paulo Guambe were shot dead in Maputo on October 19, 2024.

Mondlane remained outside the country while continuing to reject the official election result and communicate with his supporters.

He returned from self-imposed exile on January 9, 2025, six days before Chapo was due to be sworn in as president.

His return came amid heightened security concerns. Thousands of supporters gathered at Mavalane International Airport in Maputo to receive him, while police blocked access to the airport and used tear gas. Reuters reported a heavy security presence around the airport. Mondlane was allowed to enter the country and leave the airport.

The government had blamed Mondlane for inciting the unrest and said he should be held responsible for damage caused during the protests. Chapo, meanwhile, said Frelimo was open to talks with the opposition.

Mondlane continued to challenge the election result after his return. He subsequently met Chapo in Maputo on March 23 and May 20, 2025, as part of efforts to address the political crisis. The meetings did not resolve the dispute.

In July 2025, prosecutors formally charged Mondlane with the five offences now before the Supreme Court. He denied the charges.

Mondlane subsequently became a member of Mozambique’s Council of State, an advisory body to the president.

His membership became relevant to the criminal case because Council of State members have immunity.

A Council of State deliberation dated June 10, 2026, suspended Mondlane’s immunity to allow proceedings in case No 52/2025-P to continue before the Supreme Court. The decision was made public in August, after Mondlane announced that he had been notified of his trial.

Mondlane challenged the decision, arguing that the Council of State did not have the legal authority to suspend the immunity of its members.

The case could have consequences for Mondlane’s political future.

The Institute for Security Studies said in September 2025 that the charges could prevent Mondlane from contesting the 2029 presidential election.

That is not a judicial finding. Mondlane has not been convicted, and the trial has not yet taken place.

For lawyer Esau Cossa, however, the case could have consequences beyond the courtroom.

“It seems to me that he will not be imprisoned, but he will not have a clean record and will then be made ineligible to run in 2029,” Cossa told Al Jazeera.

The case could also have wider implications for public confidence in Mozambique’s justice system, particularly if it is seen as part of a broader political dispute rather than simply a criminal proceeding.

“The way the situation is evolving, the case is being perceived by society not simply as an act of justice, but as the use of justice as a political weapon. It is precisely this perception that must be avoided, because it further undermines citizens’ confidence in the institutions of justice,” Mulungo added.

articles.title: UK moves to sanction Israeli settlements as PM Burnham risks clash with Trump: report
articles.excerpt: British Ambassador Sir Christian Turner speaks with Sandra Smith about new UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and his 'leftist policies.' Turner highlights Burnham's focus on economic growth and reindustr...
articles.body_text:
British Ambassador Sir Christian Turner speaks with Sandra Smith about new UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and his 'leftist policies.' Turner highlights Burnham's focus on economic growth and reindustrializing communities, aiming for British jobs and sovereign UK strength. He underscores the critical US-UK relationship. The discussion also covers the imperative to prevent Iran from developing nuclear weapons and the need for open straits.

The United Kingdom is expected to announce restrictions targeting trade with Israeli settlements in the West Bank on Tuesday, a move already drawing strong pushback Monday from U.S. and Israeli officials.

According to The Times, a US State Department said Washington was "tracking the plans closely."

The measures are expected to include an embargo on goods and some services involving West Bank settlements marking an escalation in London’s pressure on Israel under new Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who has taken a firmer stance on the conflict, according to reports.

The announcement is expected to come a day after Burnham spoke by phone with President Donald Trump.

WHO IS ANDY BURNHAM? BRITAIN'S NEW PRIME MINISTER AND LONGTIME TRUMP CRITIC

Britain's newly appointed Prime Minister Andy Burnham delivers a speech outside 10 Downing Street after taking office, in London, Britain, July 20, 2026. (REUTERS/Temilade Adelaja)

According to a No. 10 Downing Street readout of the call Monday, the two leaders discussed the Middle East, with Burnham highlighting the importance of a two-state solution which calls for an independent Palestinian state comprising the West Bank and Gaza Strip to exist alongside Israel.

"On the Middle East, the Prime Minister set out the UK’s commitment to working towards peace and security in the region, stressing the importance of the Two-State Solution," the spokesperson said.

The readout did not mention the planned sanctions. Bloomberg reported, however, that the timing of the call suggested Burnham may have briefed Trump on the measures targeting goods and services linked to Israeli settlements in the West Bank.

The move could create an early point of friction between Burnham and Washington, where the Trump administration has strongly backed Israel, the outlet said.

I’M AN ARAB MUSLIM — I STILL DON’T UNDERSTAND THE ANTISEMITIC BDS MOVEMENT

British Energy Security and Net Zero Secretary Ed Miliband walks on Downing Street before a cabinet meeting after British Prime Minister Keir Starmer announced a timeline for his resignation, in London, Britain, June 23, 2026. (Toby Melville/Reuters)

The new measures, billed widely as sanctions, are expected to be formally unveiled by Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, who has already pledged a "comprehensive reset" of Britain’s policy toward Israeli settlements in the West Bank.

Miliband signaled last week that measures were coming in response to Israeli settlement expansion, including the E1 project east of Jerusalem, according to The National.

He went on to describe E1 as a longstanding "red line" and said Britain would take action to protect the prospect of a two-state solution.

The planned sanction announcement has already drawn sharp criticism in Israel and the United States.

Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich called for the British ambassador’s expulsion in a post on X.

"We will not be a doormat for an antisemitic government in a country occupied by radical Islam that is trying to escape economic and social collapse by attacking Jews and the State of Israel," Smotrich wrote. "The British Mandate in Israel is over."

EX-PENTAGON OFFICIAL URGES US TO ‘SQUEEZE’ UK ON DEFENSE AMID FALKLANDS FUROR

Israel's National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir arrives for a cabinet meeting at the prime minister's office in Jerusalem on Aug. 27, 2023. (MENAHEM KAHANA/Pool via REUTERS)

National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir also condemned the planned restrictions, writing in Spanish on X that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu should retaliate by recognizing Argentine sovereignty over the Falkland Islands and imposing sanctions on Britain.

Ben-Gvir accused Britain of having "violently" taken the disputed islands, known in Argentina as the Malvinas, the Times of Israel reported.

In the United States, Rep. Randy Fine, R-Fla., also warned in a post on X that the planned measures could implicate Florida’s anti-boycott law and potentially prevent some affected British companies from doing business with state and local governments.

Meanwhile, Burnham has joined leaders from Canada, France, Germany, Italy and other countries in condemning Israel’s E1 settlement expansion, arguing that the project threatens the viability of a future Palestinian state.

Emma Bussey is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital. Before joining Fox, she worked at The Telegraph with the U.S. overnight team, across desks including foreign, politics, news, sport and culture.

articles.title: EU pledges more than $200m to Greenland amid Trump annexation threats
articles.excerpt: The European Union has signed a declaration with resource-rich Greenland, promising a stronger partnership and announcing a $232m (200 million-euro) investment package to soothe anxiety caused by repe...
articles.body_text:
The European Union has signed a declaration with resource-rich Greenland, promising a stronger partnership and announcing a $232m (200 million-euro) investment package to soothe anxiety caused by repeated threats from US President Donald Trump to annex the self-governing Danish territory.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced the package, aimed at improving local quality of life over the next two years, during a visit to the Greenlandic capital Nuuk on Monday.

The EU shifted its focus towards Greenland, seeking increased cooperation with the Arctic island, following Trump’s push for greater US control of the semi-autonomous territory. His persistent threats, citing national security concerns, resulted in pushback from Greenland and Denmark and strained relationships with NATO allies.

“Greenland’s future is for the people of Greenland and Denmark to decide. No one else,” von der Leyen said.

The EU-Greenland declaration was signed by von der Leyen, Greenlandic Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen and Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen in Nuuk.

The investment package will go to Greenland’s government to strengthen administrative capability and planned programmes promoting sustainable tourism and housing construction.

Von der Leyen said the EU aims to be “more present and more engaged” in the region. Brussels has proposed doubling direct EU aid to Greenland to 530 million euros ($616m) under the bloc’s next budget for the 2028–2034 period.

Her visit coincided with the start of NATO’s Arctic Shield military exercise, bringing together soldiers from 11 countries of the alliance. The exercise will involve about 400 NATO military personnel in Greenland and will run from September 7 to 18.

“Through these challenging times, your support to us is unfailing,” Nielsen said. “You have stood by us and continue to stand by us. We feel it and are deeply grateful.”

“Greenland needs the European Union, and the European Union needs Greenland,” he added.

In January, eight European countries, including Denmark, sent a small group of military personnel to Greenland for public military exercises to show support for the island’s sovereignty and strengthen Arctic security.

Trump responded to the public military display by threatening tariffs on the countries, including Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden, and the United Kingdom. The US president backed down in February after NATO agreed to expand its military operations in the Arctic.

At the height of the crisis, Trump would not rule out using force to seize the territory of 57,000 inhabitants, sowing anxiety within the EU and NATO.

articles.title: IAEA warns over Iran nuclear access as Western powers push UN referral
articles.excerpt: France, Germany, the UK and the US are pressing the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) to report Iran to the UN Security Council, as the nuclear watchdog warns that it remains unable to verify ...
articles.body_text:
France, Germany, the UK and the US are pressing the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) to report Iran to the UN Security Council, as the nuclear watchdog warns that it remains unable to verify Tehran’s nuclear material more than a year after losing access to key facilities.

IAEA chief Rafael Grossi told the agency’s Board of Governors on Monday that Tehran had provided no information during the latest reporting period on the status of its declared nuclear material or facilities, and inspectors had been unable to conduct on-site verification.

“It is more than a year since the Agency lost continuity of knowledge” over previously declared stocks of uranium enriched to as much as 60 percent at facilities hit in US and Israeli attacks in June 2025, Grossi said.

He described the lack of information and access as a proliferation concern that “needs to be rectified with the utmost urgency”, calling on Iran to restore effective cooperation with the IAEA.

The nuclear watchdog’s warning comes as the four Western powers seek support for a draft resolution at the 35-member board that would send the Iran issue back to the UN Security Council (UNSC) for the first time in two decades, according to Reuters.

The proposed text asks Grossi to transmit the resolution, previous board decisions and his latest report to the UNSC and General Assembly. It also calls on Iran to provide the information and access required by inspectors.

Iran has rejected the move and maintains that its nuclear programme is peaceful.

Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said Western governments were again turning to the IAEA after failing to achieve their objectives elsewhere.

“Whenever they run out of options, they turn to the agency and Grossi,” Baghaei said at his weekly news conference on Monday.

He argued that restrictions facing inspectors were a consequence of US and Israeli attacks on Iranian nuclear facilities and that it was unreasonable for those governments to blame Tehran for the resulting loss of access.

Baghaei warned that Iran would take “necessary measures” if the Western powers pursued the resolution.

The draft has not yet been formally submitted to the board, and negotiations over its wording are continuing. Even if it is approved, any concrete action at the Security Council could face opposition from Russia and China, two of the five permanent veto powers.

articles.title: FSU-SMU game turns into old-school football after stadium power outage wipes out in-game communication
articles.excerpt: Just when we thought the college football weekend couldn’t get any crazier, a power outage at Doak Campbell Stadium on the campus of Florida State sent school officials into a frenzy on Monday night i...
articles.body_text:
Just when we thought the college football weekend couldn’t get any crazier, a power outage at Doak Campbell Stadium on the campus of Florida State sent school officials into a frenzy on Monday night in Tallahassee.

Minutes before SMU and FSU were set to close out Labor Day weekend with there ACC game to finish week one, the lights went out inside the stadium that forced both teams back into the locker room.

The game was scheduled to kickoff at 7:39 p.m. ET, but a power surge sent the stadium into darkness just as both teams had taking the field.

Trust me, the jokes could write themselves for Florida State, but this unfortunate set of circumstances for everyone involved turned into a chaotic night.

A very critical decision awaited, knowing there would also be no official replay during the game if both schools decided to play

Head Coach Mike Norvell of the Florida State Seminoles stands on the field before a game against the SMU Mustangs at Doak S. Campbell Stadium on Bobby Bowden Field in Tallahassee, Fla., on Sept. 7, 2026. (Getty Images)

Every twenty minutes, officials from both schools and ACC commissioner Jim Phillips were meeting to discuss possible outcomes if they weren’t able to play the game on Monday night.

For the fans, credit to them for sticking around through the madness, with games being played in the stands and the Florida State marching band trying their best to keep them all engaged. But, this was a mess.

At 8:45 ET, following a third meeting between officials, the decision was made to play the game on Monday night without any type of communications. This included helmet-to-helmet comms, communication between coordinators or iPad usage along the sideline.

A general view from the 50-yard line inside Doak S. Campbell Stadium on Bobby Bowden Field before Florida State hosted No. 19 SMU in Tallahassee, Fla., on Sept. 7, 2026. (Getty Images)

Simply put, both teams decided to go full old-school tonight in Tallahassee.

MICHIGAN-WESTERN MICHIGAN CLOCK CONTROVERSY LEAVES PLAYERS, FANS AND A RULES ANALYST PUZZLED

The officials were having to practice hand signals with the coaches from both teams at 9:06 p.m. ET, while stadium officials were praying that the power would be fully-restored by the second half at the very least.

I've seen some things covering this sport, but tonight is up their on the list on wildest events that have taken place in the past twenty years on the field.

Both teams decided it would be a wise move to play without communications that are key for everyone involved in a college football game.

And, sources told OutKick that there would have been an ample amount of problems for SMU to play this game on Tuesday. The Mustangs host UC Davis on Saturday, while the Seminoles have the weekend off.

Head coach Rhett Lashlee of the SMU Mustangs stands on the sidelines prior to a game against the Florida State Seminoles at Doak S. Campbell Stadium on Bobby Bowden Field on Sept. 7, 2026, in Tallahassee, Fla. (Getty Images)

So, pushing this game back a day might have been the smart move, but would have been challenging for Rhett Lashlee and his football program. Also, you cannot just reschedule the game for later in the season for obvious reasons.

The outcome was crucial for Florida State head coach Mike Norvell, who was already feeling the heat coming into the season.

SEC LAWYERS, LANE KIFFIN AND DEATH VALLEY: COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S WEEK 1 IS SET FOR FIREWORKS

SMU head coach Rhett Lashlee noted that his team had not practiced without coach-to-player communication in over two years, so tonight was the first time since 2024 that he had not been in communication with his quarterback during a game.

Even though both teams were dealing with the same problems Monday night, the result of this decision to play was going to haunt one of these coaches.

In the end, this might have been fun for the fans inside Doak Campbell Stadium and those watching at home.

But this was a massive gamble for SMU and Florida State to play this game Monday night, with so much on the line.

Trey Wallace is the Sr. College Sports Reporter for OutKick.

articles.body_text:
Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A popular Egyptian TV host on Saturday was sentenced to death by hanging in a major drug case that accused dozens of suspects of forming an organized criminal group to manufacture and traffic synthetic drugs.

Sarah Khalifa is among 12 defendants facing execution for their alleged roles in the operation, including importing materials used to produce narcotics, according to state-backed media Ahram Online. Capital punishment in Egypt is carried out by hanging for civilian convictions.

Khalifa is a media personality, beauty clinic owner and former TV host who has appeared on several Egyptian television channels. Local outlet Masrawy reported that she previously hosted the Egyptian crime show "Mission Impossible."

Khalifa, who currently has more than 2.5 million followers on Instagram, was reportedly arrested in Cairo in April 2025 as part of the investigation.

DOCTOR AND SON ACCUSED OF RUNNING DANGEROUS SIDE-BUSINESS SCHEME IN NEW YORK

Sara Khalifa has more than 2.5 million Instagram followers. She was arrested in Cairo in April 2025. (@sara_khaliifa/Instagram)

The case involved a total of 28 defendants who were charged with forming an organized criminal group, as well as possessing unlicensed firearms and ammunition, Ahram Online said. Twelve were sentenced to death, nine received life sentences and seven were acquitted of all charges.

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION CRACKS DOWN ON BRAZIL'S BIGGEST DRUG GANGS WITH ‘GLOBAL TERROR’ DESIGNATION

The media personality and beauty clinic owner was among 12 defendants handed death sentences in Egypt. (@sara_khaliifa/Instagram)

The group allegedly operated like a production and distribution network, with members assigned different roles. Some were responsible for importing raw materials, while others manufactured and distributed the synthetic drugs, the prosecution said, according to reports.

The group was also accused of storing materials and manufacturing drugs in a residential property.

More than 750 kilograms, or roughly 1,653 pounds, of synthetic narcotics and raw materials were seized during the investigation, prosecutors said, according to reports.

The case against Khalifa and the other defendants relied on statements from 20 witnesses, along with technical and digital evidence, including messages, photographs and videos that prosecutors said documented the alleged criminal activity, according to Ahram Online.

Khalifa was one of 12 defendants sentenced to death in a case involving alleged drug manufacturing, trafficking and firearms violations. (@sara_khaliifa/Instagram)

Authorities also placed the defendants' assets and bank accounts under precautionary measures and ordered those already in custody to remain detained, Ahram Online reported.

Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

The t...
articles.body_text:
Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

Officials in Colorado said a climber suffered a fatal fall Sunday after scaling a towering peak south of Aspen.

The tragic incident occurred on Castle Peak, which reaches a steep elevation of 14,272 feet in the Elk Mountains, according to Mountain Rescue Aspen.

Responders said rescue team members reached the climber by 4 p.m. after the Gunnison County Sheriff's Office was notified of a fallen climber.

However, officials "determined the individual had sustained injuries that were not survivable."

NORTH CAROLINA CLIMBER AIRLIFTED AFTER PLUNGING 20 FEET DOWN GORGE, SUSTAINING SERIOUS INJURIES

Responders reached the climber by 4 p.m. but determined the injuries could not be survived. (Mountain Rescue Aspen)

The fall was apparently witnessed by nearby hikers, including Rebecca Rees, who recounted the incident in a statement posted to Facebook.

"Unfortunately, we witnessed the event. It has been an extremely sad and terrible afternoon for all involved. He did not survive," she said.

Rees said a bystander, identified as Robert, even scrambled toward the climber immediately after the fall, putting himself at risk in case there was still a chance of survival.

She added that the victim ultimately "wasn’t alone" in his final moments.

NOVICE CLIMBER SURVIVES 1,500-FOOT DROP ON CALIFORNIA'S MOUNT SHASTA AFTER HELICOPTER RESCUE DELAYED BY CLOUDS

Nearby hikers reportedly witnessed the fall at Castle Peak, south of Aspen. (Mountain Rescue Aspen)

Rees said the rescue crew responded at a commendable speed. Despite the remote location, helicopter and ground teams reportedly reached nearly 13,000 feet in under two hours on a holiday weekend.

According to Mountain Rescue Aspen, officials used off-highway vehicles and helicopters to reach the remote area.

After a helicopter located the fallen climber, it returned to Aspen to pick up additional rescue personnel before taking them to the high-elevation area near the peak.

MOUNTAIN CLIMBER SURVIVES TERRIFYING 500-FOOT FALL IN CALIFORNIA'S SIERRA NEVADA, NIGHT STRANDED ON LEDGE

Officials said the climber was recovered from the mountain shortly after 8 p.m. (Mountain Rescue Aspen)

A total of 21 rescue members were sent into the field, and officials safely recovered and evacuated the deceased climber from the mountain shortly after 8 p.m.

Rees said the responders showed extraordinary compassion throughout the recovery effort.

The rescue operation unfolded at elevations approaching 13,000 feet. (Mountain Rescue Aspen)

"The response of search and rescue, the sheriff, and the coroner all made us feel like every single person matters. This young man had a story and we all care," she said.

Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

articles.title: Panama Canal may cut ship traffic further as El Niño strengthens
articles.excerpt: Panama could impose further cuts on the number of ships sailing through the Panama Canal, an official said, as a strengthening El Niño raises fears of water shortages at one of the world’s busiest mar...
articles.body_text:
Panama could impose further cuts on the number of ships sailing through the Panama Canal, an official said, as a strengthening El Niño raises fears of water shortages at one of the world’s busiest maritime trade routes.

The warning from the new administrator of the Panama Canal Authority, Ilya Espino de Marotta, on Monday came after the government declared a nationwide state of emergency over El Niño on August 26.

The canal, which handles 5 percent of global maritime trade, has already reduced the maximum number of ships allowed through daily, from 36 last month to 34 starting on September 4.

A further reduction will start on September 15, when the limit will be 32 ships.

Espino, who took over as administrator of the Panama Canal Authority on Monday, told the AFP news agency that restrictions could be tightened again if the drought does not subside.

She said she was not ruling out the possibility that in February or March, the limits “could be reduced to 29 or something similar”.

She said rainfall over the coming months would determine whether further restrictions are needed.

“Depending on how much rain falls in September, October and November – the three critical months – that will determine whether I need to lower any slots further in January, February or March,” she told the Reuters news agency last week.

The restrictions are not expected to become as severe as during the 2023-24 drought, when daily crossings fell as low as 22.

The Panama Canal depends on freshwater to operate the locks that raise and lower vessels travelling between the Atlantic and Pacific oceans. Water comes mainly from the artificial Gatun and Alajuela lakes, which are replenished by rainfall.

An average transit consumes about 200 million litres (about 53 million gallons) of water.

That dependence makes the 80km (50-mile) canal particularly vulnerable to prolonged dry weather, and levels in both reservoirs have already dropped with the onset of El Niño.

This year’s El Niño – which affects weather patterns and pushes up global temperatures – is expected to be the strongest since record-keeping began four decades ago.

Apart from reducing the number of vessels transiting the Panama Canal, authorities have also reduced their maximum draft, from 15.2 metres to 14.6 metres (50 feet to 48 feet).

Draft ⁠is the depth of water a ship needs to float safely. A lower draft limit means vessels may have to carry less cargo to pass through the canal.

The disruption comes at a sensitive time for global shipping.

The Panama Canal’s importance has increased as traffic through the Strait of Hormuz in the Middle East has fallen sharply amid the US-Israel war on Iran. Some vessels have recently paid more than $1m at auction to secure transit ‌slots through the canal.

Panama is betting on a new reservoir at Rio Indio – a river in the country’s centre – as a longer-term solution.

The project is intended to provide water for canal operations and more than half of Panama’s population for the next 50 years, but it is expected to take five to six years to complete.

Espino, the new administrator, told Reuters that the reservoir would “ensure that the canal never again has to resort to lowering the draft or reducing the number of transits”.

articles.title: Ukraine's chief prosecutor resigns over call centre corruption scandal
articles.excerpt:
Ukraine's chief prosecutor Ruslan Kravchenko has resigned over corruption allegations related to illegal call centres in the country.

It follows a search of his offices over the weekend by Ukrainian ...
articles.body_text:
Ukraine's chief prosecutor Ruslan Kravchenko has resigned over corruption allegations related to illegal call centres in the country.

It follows a search of his offices over the weekend by Ukrainian anti-corruption investigators, who said they had identified a money-laundering scheme led by an official in Kravchenko's office.

In his resignation letter, Kravchenko said he did not want his position to be used as a "tool for political confrontation", and referenced an earlier post in which he rejected the claims as "unsubstantiated".

Corruption scandals have plagued Kyiv throughout the war against Russia, with accusations levelled at several members of President Volodymyr Zelensky's inner circle.

According to Ukraine's National Anti-Corruption Bureau (Nabu) and Specialised Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office (Sap), the network in Kravchenko's office received money to protect call centres that carried out phone scams and "laundered millions in assets".

The money was then used to buy property, jewellery, and other valuables, according to Nabu.

Kravchenko released a statement on Sunday evening dismissing the allegations as "completely unsubstantiated", and denied any wrongdoing.

He tendered his resignation a day later, thanking Zelensky and the Ukrainian parliament for their "trust". The Ukrainian president is yet to comment publicly on the resignation.

Despite the creation of two Ukrainian anti-corruption bodies, Nabu and Sap, over a decade ago, corruption continues to be a significant problem in the country.

In 2025, nationwide protests broke out after Zelensky tried to implement reforms that would curb the independence of Nabu and Sap.

Kyiv's European partners expressed alarm at the announcement, with ambassadors from the G7 group of nations warning it could endanger Ukraine's integration into the European Union.

Ukraine is an EU candidate country, a status it was granted on condition it mounted a credible fight against corruption.

Zelensky reinstated the freedom of the two anti-corruption bodies as a result of the backlash, but questions have persisted over his commitment to anti-corruption reform.

Last month, Nabu said it had uncovered a scheme to misappropriate more than $3m (£2.2m) in Ukrainian currency to pay bail for a former energy minister accused of money laundering.

A senior official in Zelensky's office alleged to be involved was sacked.

Fedorov asked about Ukraine government corruption claims

In an interview with the BBC last month, Ukraine's former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov said the president needed to be asked about his awareness of potential corruption among his closest team.

"Let him answer this question... I believe that he's ready for such questions. It's his responsibility to tell us all whether he was aware of all that or not... I don't want to make any assumptions," he said.

During his time in office, the 35-year-old was credited with heading a drive against corruption.

Since his dismissal in mid-July, after reportedly falling out with the head of Ukraine's armed forces, he has been outspoken against what he has called a "systemic crisis of governance" in Ukraine.

However, he has emphasised that he has no evidence that Zelensky is personally involved in corruption.

"In all the time that I worked with him, not a single time have I received from him any task or assignment that would go against law or my sense of integrity," Federov told the BBC.

Zelensky should be asked what he knew about government corruption, sacked minister tells BBC

Major corruption scandal engulfs top Zelensky allies

articles.title: Aaron Judge returns to Yankees after 83 games missed with rib injury ahead of postseason push
articles.excerpt:
Alanna Rizzo shares her thoughts on the MLB post-season.

The Bronx Bombers are getting their captain back.

Aaron Judge is making his long-awaited return from the 60-day injured list, as the New York...
articles.body_text:
Alanna Rizzo shares her thoughts on the MLB post-season.

The Bronx Bombers are getting their captain back.

Aaron Judge is making his long-awaited return from the 60-day injured list, as the New York Yankees announced his reinstatement ahead of their series against the Colorado Rockies on Tuesday night at Yankee Stadium.

Judge has spent the last three months on the injured list with a stress fracture in his right first rib, which he suffered in late May.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

New York Yankees' Aaron Judge rounds the bases after hitting a solo home run in the third inning against the Texas Rangers in Arlington, Texas, on April 27, 2026. (Tony Gutierrez/AP)

On Monday, Judge was seen working out at Yankee Stadium, facing live batting practice and hitting the ball all over the field, indicating he was healthy enough to go against big league arms.

In fact, the Yankees opted not to give Judge a minor-league rehab assignment. Manager Aaron Boone noted there were more creative ways to build Judge’s stamina for a postseason run in September, which includes potentially playing in games with the Yankees and being pulled before nine innings are complete.

Judge has been working his way back since he was cleared to do baseball activities in August. He was simply hitting off a tee, or getting soft toss, before he could take real batting practice on the field. He was seen in San Diego with the team during their West Coast road trip hitting before games.

JAZZ CHISHOLM JR SAYS KNICKS CHAMPIONSHIP PARADE FUELS HIS WORLD SERIES HUNGER WITH YANKEES

Judge has also been facing a high-velocity pitching machine, while doing outfield and baserunning drills to increase his stamina and get him ready for his role in right field once again.

Either way, the Yankees get back their three-time MVP outfielder and a key cog in their hopes of returning to the World Series.

New York Yankees outfielder Aaron Judge (99) connects for a base hit against the Boston Red Sox during the first inning of Game 1 of an American League Wild Card baseball playoff series, Tuesday, Sept. 30, 2025, in New York. (AP Photo/Frank Franklin II)

New York is still four games behind the AL East-leading Tampa Bay Rays, but they own the top American League Wild Card slot with a nine-game lead heading into Tuesday’s start against the Rockies. At 81-62, the Yankees will be gunning for that top spot in the East, especially considering the winner of it will likely own the top AL playoff spot for the postseason.

The Boston Red Sox are also right behind the Yankees at 80-65 thus far.

Judge was hitting .248/.375/.533 with 17 homers and 38 RBI before hitting the injured list on June 5. The Yankees went 45-38 in the 83 games he’s missed.

New York Yankees' Aaron Judge, who is injured, runs drills in the outfield before a baseball game between the New York Yankees and Tampa Bay Rays, Thursday, July 31, 2025, in New York. (AP Photo/Heather Khalifa)

While the offense struggled to pick up the slack left by Judge, the pitching staff has been stellar throughout his absence. Thus, Judge’s return couldn’t be coming at a better time for the Yankees, as they hope to match their pitching prowess with more consistent offense during this final regular-season push.

Scott Thompson is a sports writer for Fox News Digital.
