articles.title: Indiana QB Josh Hoover delivers the greatest "football guy" moment of the season so far
articles.excerpt:
Josh Hoover connected with Charlie Becker for a nine-yard TD, extending the Indiana Hoosiers' lead over the North Texas Mean Green.

Football is tough. Football is not for the faint of heart or for th...
articles.body_text:
Josh Hoover connected with Charlie Becker for a nine-yard TD, extending the Indiana Hoosiers' lead over the North Texas Mean Green.

Football is tough. Football is not for the faint of heart or for the weak of body. TCU transfer and Indiana Hoosiers QB Josh Hoover proved that in the first half of his debut against North Texas.

Halfway through the second quarter Hoover dropped back to pass and North Texas defensive lineman Udoka Ezeani took a hold of Hoover's facemask, completely spinning the facemask to the back of his head. It was one of the worst and most blatant facemasks you'll ever see. The play caused Hoover to bleed profusely, yet he stayed in the game.

Shortly after that vicious facemask, the Fox Big Noon Saturday crew showed a close-up of Hoover looking like he just went 15 rounds like Ivan Drago. With his eyes half open and face bloodied, broadcaster Gus Johnson said, "Welcome to Indiana. He bleeds red."

Indiana Hoosiers quarterback Josh Hoover drops back to pass during the second quarter of a college football game against the North Texas Mean Green on Sept. 5, 2026, at Memorial Stadium in Bloomington, Ind. (Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

STAY "FEARLESS" ON THE GO! TAKE TOMI LAHREN WITH YOU. DOWNLOAD THE TLIF PODCAST NOW!

Three plays after the penalty, with blood pouring down his nose, dripping from his chinstrap and facemask, Hoover delivered a dart to arguably his favorite target, wide receiver Charlie Becker for a 9-yard touchdown.

Indiana Hoosiers wide receiver Charlie Becker catches a pass for a touchdown against the North Texas Mean Green on Sept. 5, 2026, at Memorial Stadium in Bloomington, Ind. (Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

Hoover could be seen with blood all over his pants, face, and jersey. It was everywhere. He proved that this is why we love the game of football so much. College football is delivering in a major way in week one and I'm here for it.

Indiana Hoosiers unveil National Champions 2025 signage in Memorial Stadium in Bloomington, Ind., before a game against North Texas on Sept. 5, 2026. (Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

Hoover has some big shoes to fill following Heisman Trophy winner Fernando Mendoza, and a program coming off a National Championship. He finished the first half nearly perfect, completing 7 of 8 pass attempts for 100 yards and 2 touchdowns.

Jon is a writer and content creator for OutKick

articles.title: Cuban and Afghan immigrants deported from US under Trump arrive in Guyana
articles.excerpt:
Guyana says that it has received six people deported from the United States, as the administration of President Donald Trump steps up so-called third-country deportations.

Guyana’s Foreign Secretary ...
articles.body_text:
Guyana says that it has received six people deported from the United States, as the administration of President Donald Trump steps up so-called third-country deportations.

Guyana’s Foreign Secretary Robert Persaud announced that a group of Cuban and Afghan nationals had arrived in the South American nation on Saturday, after being deported due to immigration issues.

“The US has not made any further requests” for non-citizen deportations to be sent to Guyana at this time, Persaud told The Associated Press news agency.

None had criminal backgrounds, according to Persaud. The removals are part of an ongoing campaign under Trump, who promised during his 2024 re-election bid to engineer the “largest deportation programme of criminals in the history of America”.

Persaud said that Guyana reached an agreement with the US to receive deportees after months of negotiations.

The human rights nonprofit Amnesty International estimates that more than 30 countries have entered into such agreements since Trump returned to office, including 15 in the Americas region.

The deal with Guyana will last for one year and does not constitute permanent resettlement, Persaud said.

Third-country deportations involve sending foreign nationals to places outside of their country of origin. Deportees often have no familiarity with the country they are sent to and sometimes do not even speak the language.

The Trump administration has sought to expand the use of third-country deportations.

It has struck agreements with a range of countries around the world, including several as far afield as Africa. Some of the deals have involved multimillion-dollar payments.

Trump officials have justified the effort by arguing that some countries, such as Cuba, refuse to accept deportees from the US.

Rights groups, however, have denounced the practice as an effort to punish migrants and pressure them into giving up their immigration claims in the US.

Many of the deportees have no criminal background, reflecting the expanding scope of Trump’s deportation efforts during his second term.

The Transactional Records Access Clearinghouse (TRAC), a research organisation at Syracuse University, estimates that 70.6 percent of foreign nationals currently in US immigration detention have no criminal conviction.

Third-country deportations have also raised concerns about conditions in the countries non-citizens are sent to. Some countries struggle with poverty, instability and conflict, as well as human rights abuses.

The deportees sent to Guyana on Saturday will receive resources through the Assisted Voluntary Return Programme, run by the United Nations International Organisation for Migration (IOM).

Under the arrangement, those deported will await the outcome of their immigration process in Guyana.

They could return to their countries of origin or seek relocation elsewhere.

Efforts to restrict immigration, deport foreign nationals and crack down on civil immigration infractions have become a hallmark of Trump’s second term.

As part of that campaign, the Trump administration has stripped tens of thousands of migrants in the country of their legal status, through the cancellation of programmes like Temporary Protected Status or humanitarian parole.

Reports have also emerged that the administration plans to strip visas from roughly 200,000 people seeking asylum.

The removal of their legal immigration status exposes foreign nationals to the risk of deportation, in some cases despite ongoing conflicts or unstable conditions in their destination countries.

Duniam says they want smoking rates to go down, and “part of the problem is dealing with cheap smokes out there in the community”.

Killing off the illegal trade is the only way to do that, he says, but concedes it’s difficult to model the effects in an unregulated industry.

Excise cut modelling ‘saw a real change’, Duniam says.

Jessica Hull finished third in the 1500m event.

Oh, Sydney. I have only just caught up with the fact you got to 33C yesterday. But also snow in the south of the state?

Good morning, all – Tory Shepherd here to kick off your Sunday. Happy Father’s Day if that is a happy time for you, and if (like me) it’s a bit of a sad one, I see you.

articles.title: Fuel tanker blast in western Iran kills at least 10
articles.excerpt:
At least 10 people were killed in a fuel tanker blast in western Iran, Iranian national broadcast media (IRIB) reported.

The tanker explosion on Saturday was triggered by a road crash on the Hamedan-...
articles.body_text:
At least 10 people were killed in a fuel tanker blast in western Iran, Iranian national broadcast media (IRIB) reported.

The tanker explosion on Saturday was triggered by a road crash on the Hamedan-Sanandaj highway.

The accident was caused by a technical fault in the braking system of the vehicle carrying the tanker, said the governor of Sanandaj, the capital of Iran’s Kurdistan province, as reported by the Reuters news agency.

At least six other people were injured in the incident, the governor also said, adding that casualty figures were based on initial reports.

According to local officials, the resulting fire was immediately brought under control. They did not provide further details on the identities of those killed.

The latest deadly accident adds to a long history of deadly tanker and bus collisions in Iran, where poor road conditions, ageing vehicle fleets and heavy freight traffic have made such accidents a recurring hazard.

At least 13 people were killed in 2018, after a fuel tanker slammed into a bus that had stopped to pick up passengers near Sanandaj.

UNICEF said Iran’s rate of traffic crashes is 20 times the world’s average, as the country suffers from poor roads and lax traffic enforcement.

According to a May 2017 report by the Tehran-based newspaper Financial Tribune, more than 20,000 people are killed and 800,000 are injured annually in road accidents in Iran.

articles.title: Fan runs onto field at Houston Cougars game, gets absolutely trucked by police officer
articles.excerpt: "I'm sad about this because I think college football was more interesting when Colorado had Shedeur Sanders and Travis Hunter and Deion was fresh, but they crashed last year. Three and nine, five game...
articles.body_text:
"I'm sad about this because I think college football was more interesting when Colorado had Shedeur Sanders and Travis Hunter and Deion was fresh, but they crashed last year. Three and nine, five game losing streak they're currently on. Seems like there's a lot of things. Dion's health, that kind of thing. I don't know, man. This seems to be headed in a bad direction. And as importantly, I guess it's not interesting anymore."

The college football season, in all its glory, is upon us, and it feels like it couldn’t have come soon enough for all of us.

In fact, a lunatic in Houston couldn't wait more than one game before sprinting onto the field.

Unfortunately for him — but fortunately for the rest of us — he was absolutely demolished by a police officer who was at the top of his game.

HERE'S WHY, EVEN WITH ALL ITS PROBLEMS, COLLEGE FOOTBALL IS STILL BETTER THAN THE NFL

A fan who ran onto the field during Saturday's Houston Cougars game against the Oregon State Beavers sees his life flash before his eyes as a police officer gets him lined up for a tackle. (Photo by Austin McAfee/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

The No. 23 Cougars opened their season with one of the tougher Week 1 matchups, with the Oregon State Beavers coming to town.

Houston ended up winning 33-20 to go 1-0 in this young college football season, but they didn't get the job done before some dude in a blue shirt hopped on the field to... actually, I'm not really sure what he was trying to accomplish.

UMASS PLAYER ABSOLUTELY OBLITERATES UNSUSPECTING WOMAN ON THE SIDELINES AFTER INTERCEPTION

Jeez! That's some top-notch work from the boys in blue.

I think Houston’s going to get calls asking how many more years of eligibility that cop has left because that tackle was textbook.

I still don't understand why people do this. Sure, you get a few moments of fleeting face time on social media, but at what cost?

Getting driven through the Earth's crust by a cop or security guard who definitely played at least a year or two of college ball?

INDIANA'S MASCOT STARTS THE SEASON WITH AN ABSOLUTE HEATER THAT PUTS OTHER MASCOTS TO SHAME

A police officer delivers a textbook tackle to a fan who ran onto the field on Saturday in Houston. (Photo by Austin McAfee/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

Well, he'll be feeling that one tomorrow, and probably for several days after.

I'm sure he's not thinking about doing that again, but on the off chance that he is, the next time the Cougars are in action will be on Sept. 12, when they host the Southern Jaguars.

The following week, they'll have what is shaping up to be a huge game for the Big XII championship picture when they travel to Lubbock to take on Texas Tech.

articles.title: Trump-backed group announces $10m ad spend for midterm Senate race in Texas
articles.excerpt: A political group associated with United States President Donald Trump has announced it will spend $10m on television and digital advertisements in the state of Texas ahead of the upcoming midterm ele...
articles.body_text:
A political group associated with United States President Donald Trump has announced it will spend $10m on television and digital advertisements in the state of Texas ahead of the upcoming midterm elections.

The Saturday filing with the Federal Election Commission (FEC) represents the first major spend in a general election by MAGA, Inc, a super PAC named for Trump’s “Make America Great Again” movement.

The advertisements are expected to heavily target Democratic candidate James Talarico, a 37-year-old state representative running for the US Senate against Trump-backed Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton.

Speculation abounds that Democrats may have a chance of flipping one of Texas’s Senate seats for the first time since 1993.

Paxton has weathered a series of scandals, even facing a state impeachment trial. Still, Democrats have repeatedly faced withering defeats in Texas, having failed to win a statewide office there in more than three decades.

In a statement on Saturday, MAGA, Inc sought to portray Talarico as out of touch with everyday Texans.

“High Tax Talarico wants to take money out of Texans’ pockets,” spokesperson Alex Pfeiffer said. “MAGA Inc is going to ensure Texas knows about Talarico’s radical policies and elects Ken Paxton to the US Senate.”

While Texas is often seen as a Republican stronghold, Trump’s deepening unpopularity and cost-of-living concerns have bolstered Democrats like Talarico ahead of November’s midterm elections.

Republicans currently hold slim majorities in both chambers of Congress. But Democrats are hoping to flip a few key seats to break the Republicans’ hold on the legislature.

Whoever wins control of Congress will likely be able to shape the legislative agenda of Trump’s final two years as president.

The advertisements announced on Saturday will focus on tax policy, accusing Democrats of seeking tax hikes that would burden voters.

Democrats, meanwhile, have traditionally accused Republicans of awarding tax breaks to the most affluent.

That criticism re-emerged last year, when the Republican-led Congress passed Trump’s signature piece of legislation, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, along party lines.

In addition to increasing spending on Trump priorities like defence and immigration, the bill also made permanent the tax breaks Trump had debuted during his first term and increased exemptions for federal estate taxes.

Critics pointed out that those tax cuts would largely benefit wealthier earners.

In response to criticism of his economic policy, Talarico’s campaign accused the candidate’s right-wing opponents of pouring outside money into the race and misrepresenting his record.

“Billionaire-backed dark money groups are lying about James Talarico because they’re scared of the people-powered movement we’re building to fix this broken, corrupt political system,” campaign spokesperson JT Ennis said in response to Saturday’s announcement.

“James was proud to vote for the largest property tax cut in Texas history and has consistently voted to cut taxes for working Texans.”

Texas has been a focal point of Republican strategy throughout the midterm campaign season.

Last year, Trump officials petitioned Texas lawmakers to redraw the state’s congressional map in a way that gives Republicans an advantage in winning five extra seats in the House of Representatives.

After Texas followed through, other Republican-led states followed suit, with Democrats mounting similar efforts in states like California.

This week, Trump will also travel to Dallas, Texas, to headline a first-ever Republican midterm convention. He will speak at both nights of the gathering.

Trump has made himself a centrepiece of Republican strategy in the lead-up to the midterms, travelling around the country to hold rallies and support party members. “What I really want you to do is pretend, please, that I’m on the ballot,” he told a rally in South Carolina last month.

But questions have emerged about the large sum of money gathered by MAGA Inc — and whether it would be distributed to down-ballot Republican candidates.

Faced with such questions, Trump told reporters on Friday that he planned to allocate between $400m and $500m from MAGA, Inc to help Republicans in the midterms.

Trump has also used his influence to shape Republican primaries across the country, boosting his preferred candidates.

The president’s endorsement, for instance, helped Paxton defeat incumbent Senator John Cornyn in the party’s May primary, despite concerns that the attorney general’s scandals could damage his chances in the general election.

articles.title: Dr Phil says Lindsay Clancy mistrial a 'teachable moment' on postpartum psychosis: 'There was a failure here'
articles.excerpt: Medical analyst Dr. Phil McGraw discusses public division and the jury deadlock in the Lindsay Clancy murder case. McGraw warns of copycat fears and analyzes the mistrial. McGraw says Clancy should be...
articles.body_text:
Medical analyst Dr. Phil McGraw discusses public division and the jury deadlock in the Lindsay Clancy murder case. McGraw warns of copycat fears and analyzes the mistrial. McGraw says Clancy should be held 'fully accountable.'

Dr. Phil McGraw on Saturday weighed in on the Lindsay Clancy trial, one day after the judge declared a mistrial when the jurors were unable to reach a unanimous verdict in the killings of her three children.

The defense team of the mother who admitted to strangling her three children to death in 2023 claims the 36-year-old was suffering from postpartum psychosis and wasn’t in control of her actions when she killed her children.

McGraw told Fox News anchor Aishah Hasnie on "Fox News Live" Saturday that Clancy's children: Cora, 5; Dawson, 3; and Callan, 8 months, "are the real folks we need to give our attention to here. Three innocent children did lose their lives, and you can never explain these situations away simply."

PATRICK CLANCY SPEAKS OUT AFTER HUNG JURY IN LINDSAY CLANCY CASE, ADDRESSES PROSPECT OF ANOTHER TRIAL

He said it also concerns him when mental illness gets depicted in the courtroom, it becomes "kind of a political, ideological football that’s used to try to skew something or is kind of debunked by another side rather than looking at what actually took place."

McGraw stressed that there eventually will be "accountability" in the case. Even if she’s not found criminally responsible, "she’s not going home."

"She’s going to have to live with this the rest of her life and probably in a psychiatric facility if, in fact, she is not guilty by reason of mental defect or disease," he said.

He added, "I think people underestimate the power of psychosis in taking over someone’s life. It’s not an excuse, but, for example, if she had a brain tumor you could see on an X-ray, people would go ‘OK, I get that.’ And when you have what took place here, it could be just as powerful as someone whose brain is hijacked by a tumor."

LINDSAY CLANCY DESCRIBED A MALE VOICE ORDERING HER TO ‘KILL HER CHILDREN AND KILL HERSELF’: TESTIMONY

Spectators and media are lined up outside Plymouth Superior Court, Plymouth, Mass., on Thursday. (David McGlynn for Fox News Digital)

"I’m not excusing what she did in any way," he said. "I think she should be held fully accountable, but I think we need to understand causation."

The prosecution made a "pretty clunky presentation," McGraw said, adding that he felt they got their act together "in the end."

"I’ve spent a lot of my professional career working in trial sciences and dealing with juries and juries looking for a coherent explanation," he explained.

He said the defense’s explanation was "much more understandable and much more coherent than what the prosecution did.

McGraw also worried that the case could cause a "copycat" effect.

He said, "We certainly don’t want that to take place here, so we need to look at what the cultural effects are."

There is also a "huge" difference between postpartum depression and postpartum psychosis, he stressed.

ILLINOIS MOTHER CHARGED WITH MURDER IN DEATH OF 2-YEAR-OLD SON IN CASE DRAWING COMPARISONS TO LINDSAY CLANCY

Callan, left, Dawson and Cora Clancy. The three children were killed at their Duxbury, Mass., home in January 2023. (Lindsay Marie Clancy/Facebook)

"Postpartum psychosis is a psychiatric emergency that requires immediate hospitalization," he said. "It’s not a time to adjust medications, it’s not a time to schedule an extra appointment during the week. It is a psychiatric emergency that requires in-patient care and separation from the children. Not tomorrow morning, not tomorrow afternoon, but immediately."

He called Clancy’s case a "psychiatric emergency that wasn’t treated as such."

It’s one thing to use the case as a "teachable moment for the country," McGraw cautioned, adding that it’s another for people to raise her up as some kind of "heroine."

"There’s nothing to be celebrated here," he said. "If there’s any lesson to be taken for our culture, it’s that there was a failure here. This was a woman who asked for help. She admitted herself to the hospital. Was that enough?"

The jury "tends to get it right," he said, explaining that they were "headed toward committing her for a long period of time."

"I think people need to understand that mental illness is a serious, serious issue," he said, adding that he was worried that people would forget about Cora, Dawson and Callan.

ROGAN SHREDS SUPPORTERS OF LINDSAY CLANCY, SAYS THEY WOULDN'T RALLY IF A FATHER WERE ON TRIAL FOR SAME CRIME

The judge in the Lindsay Clancy case declared a mistrial on Friday. (Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger via Pool)

"I hate we are focusing everywhere except there," he said. "And there are a lot of fingers to point, but now’s not the time to do that. We need to adjudicate this case, and then we need to step back and say, ‘What can we learn from this?’

Situations like Clancy’s case "occur one or two times out of 1,000," McGraw explained, "but that’s not nothing. One or two times out of 1,000 are one or two times too many. This is avoidable."

His wish is that from this people would pay attention to the "red flags" depicted in Clancy’s case that can be "internalized to help mothers when they get in over their heads and need the kind of intervention that was needed here."

"Reach out for help," he urged. "It’s not weakness, it’s strength."

Brie Stimson is a Los Angeles-based entertainment and breaking news writer for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: In-N-Out's popular burger style started with a customer request decades ago
articles.excerpt:
California chef Andrew Gruel demonstrates how fresh and frozen burger patties stack up in flavor and texture, revealing why one earned higher marks for moisture, beefy taste and overall quality.

In-N...
articles.body_text:
California chef Andrew Gruel demonstrates how fresh and frozen burger patties stack up in flavor and texture, revealing why one earned higher marks for moisture, beefy taste and overall quality.

In-N-Out Burger is known for its simple menu, with basic burgers, fries and shakes. Yet by 2005, the fast-food chain was listing some of its most popular off-menu orders on a "Not-So-Secret Menu" online.

Among the most famous off-menu offerings is the Animal Style burger, which the company website says is a "burger of your choice with hand-leafed lettuce, tomato, a mustard-cooked beef patty; add pickle, extra spread, with grilled onions."

AMERICA'S FAVORITE FAST-FOOD CHAIN NAMED: MCDONALD'S WINS HEARTS BUT NOT BEST BURGER, SURVEY SAYS

In-N-Out’s website says the restaurants accommodate special orders because they’re "all about making our customers happy" — and that’s just how the Animal Style burger got its start.

"We began serving the Animal Style burger in the early 1960s when a customer watched one of our associates make his own customized burger and asked for one made the same way," In-N-Out Burger chief operating officer Denny Warnick told Fox News Digital.

In-N-Out's Animal Style burger (this one is a double-double) features a mustard-cooked beef patty, pickles, extra spread and grilled onions, along with lettuce and tomato. (In-N-Out/Fox News)

"The name was created there on the spot. Over the years, many of the variations in preparation for our basic menu items were given names, usually by the customers who frequently ordered their burgers that way. The terms were merely used to describe a way of preparing an order or a menu item exactly the way a customer wanted it."

Warnick said some of those names stuck, and today many customers order from the "secret" menu.

"Whether a ‘secret menu’ order or not, we still cook every burger fresh-to-order, exactly how the customer wants it," he said.

In addition to Animal Style, In-N-Out includes on its off-menu list Double-Meat, with two beef patties; the 3x3, with three beef patties and three slices of American cheese; the 4x4, which is the same as the 3x3 but with an added patty and cheese slice; the Grilled Cheese, which replaces a burger patty with two slices of American cheese; and Protein Style, which is "your favorite burger wrapped in hand-leafed lettuce instead of a bun."

Animal Style has become one of the best-known orders on In-N-Out's "Not-So-Secret Menu." (iStock)

Founders Harry and Esther Snyder opened the first In-N-Out in a suburb of Los Angeles, Calif., in 1948. According to the company’s website, it was California’s first drive-thru hamburger stand.

By 1973, there were 13 restaurants open, all in Los Angeles County.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Today, the company is still privately owned by the Snyder family, and there are more than 400 locations in 10 states.

The off-menu options have been an open secret for decades.

Many of In-N-Out's named off-menu preparations grew out of the ways customers customized their orders, according to the company. (Paul Bersebach/MediaNews Group/Orange County Register via Getty Images)

The Los Angeles Times reported in 2004 that In-N-Out customers had known about ordering their burgers Animal Style "for years."

"Relish the not-so-secret menu," the Times advised in 2005, noting that customers could find the secret menu on In-N-Out’s website and suggesting they try their burgers Animal Style and fries well done.

"Then try to find the little Bible verse references hidden in the wrappers and stamped under the cups – a fun game if you’re trying to sober up from an evening out," the Times added.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Though Animal Style is quite well known by now, the special burger is still attracting new converts.

"Got my burger Animal Style for the first time," a Redditor wrote on a subreddit two years ago. "It honestly was a game changer and is my new order. I don’t think I will ever go back."

"From LA. My parents have been going to [In-N-Out] long before I was born, and they just learned about Animal Style a month ago," another user responded. "I couldn’t believe my frickin ears."

In-N-Out says its first location, opened in 1948, was California's first drive-thru hamburger stand. (iStock)

Another off-menu order not listed on In-N-Out’s online menu is the Flying Dutchman — two patties and two cheese slices without buns or condiments — which the company says on its history page was created by former CEO Guy Snyder before he died in 1999.

Teresa Mull is a freelance writer with the Lifestyle team at Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Drone attack blamed on guerrillas kills at least three soldiers in Colombia
articles.excerpt:
Officials accuse National Liberation Army of launching strike followed by clash inside military compound

An attack involving explosives dropped from drones followed by a clash inside a military compo...
articles.body_text:
Officials accuse National Liberation Army of launching strike followed by clash inside military compound

An attack involving explosives dropped from drones followed by a clash inside a military compound in north-eastern Colombia has killed at least three soldiers and wounded four, Colombia’s army said on Saturday.

Local authorities blamed the attack – which took place late on Friday – on the rebel National Liberation Army (ELN).

It targeted a military unit in the municipality of Ocaña, in the Norte de Santander department, which borders Venezuela. Two soldiers died at the site and a third after receiving medical attention, Colombia’s military said on X.

Colombia’s president, Abelardo de la Espriella, condemned the attack. “For every police officer or soldier murdered, we will bring the full weight and legitimate force of the state down upon the criminals,” he said.

Much of ELN, an armed group active since 1964, is based in the Catatumbo region, which includes parts of the Norte de Santander and Cesar departments. ELN also harbours dissident factions of the now defunct Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (Farc) that did not join the peace agreement a decade ago.

Both groups are vying for control of the strategic region, which connects to the porous border with Venezuela and is one of Colombia’s primary coca-producing areas.

In August, an explosion outside a police station in Cucuta injured 11 police officers and killed a police dog. Officials also blamed that attack on the ELN.

Earlier this week, at least one civilian was killed and 11 other people were injured after a car bomb exploded outside a police station in north-eastern Colombia.

articles.title: Prince William to represent King Charles at funeral of Norway’s King Harald V
articles.excerpt:
Duty falls by precedent to William to attend service of late monarch, alongside Princess Royal, who is godmother to new king Haakon VIII

The Prince of Wales is to represent his father at the funeral ...
articles.body_text:
Duty falls by precedent to William to attend service of late monarch, alongside Princess Royal, who is godmother to new king Haakon VIII

The Prince of Wales is to represent his father at the funeral of King Harald V of Norway next week, Buckingham Palace has announced.

William, the heir to the throne, will be joined by his aunt the Princess Royal, who is attending in a private and personal capacity as godmother of the new king, Haakon VIII.

Norway has seen an outpouring of grief for the much-loved late monarch, who died on 28 August at the age of 89.

Harald has been hailed as an inclusive “people’s king” who modernised the Norwegian monarchy during his 35-year reign.

His funeral will take place on 9 September at Oslo Cathedral, with mourners including his widow, Sonja, now the queen mother.

In keeping with precedent that the sovereign does not attend funerals of other heads of state, the duty falls to William, a future king, to represent his father and pay his respects at the service.

Charles paid a touching tribute to his “dear cousin” and “much-loved kinsman and friend” after the news of Harald’s death was announced.

In a message of condolence, he praised Harald’s “unwavering dedication” and his “kindness, compassion and deep sense of duty echoed from across the sea and across the decades”.

The late Queen Elizabeth II and King Harald were second cousins. They shared the same great-grandparents, King Edward VII and Queen Alexandra.

In April last year, William represented his father at the funeral of Pope Francis in the Vatican.

William and the now Princess of Wales carried out an official tour to Norway in 2018, dining with King Harald and Queen Sonja at the Royal Palace, where Harald described them as “family” and praised their support of the then Queen.

The Norwegian sovereign processed into the banquet arm in arm with the pregnant Catherine, who was expecting Prince Louis and wearing a flowing Alexander McQueen gown, with the gesture mirrored by Sonja and William who walked behind them.

William and Kate also spent time visiting the ski slopes with the then Crown Prince Haakon and Crown Princess Mette-Marit, now the King and Queen.

articles.title: More voters identifying as Democrats and not calling themselves Republican
articles.excerpt:
Latest data from Gallup, showing 49% leaning Democrat and 39% Republican, marks sharp reversal from 2024

More voters are identifying as Democrats and shying away from calling themselves Republican, a...
articles.body_text:
Latest data from Gallup, showing 49% leaning Democrat and 39% Republican, marks sharp reversal from 2024

More voters are identifying as Democrats and shying away from calling themselves Republican, according to the latest quarterly data published by Gallup.

Some 49% of voters surveyed leaned Democrat, including independent voters asked to pick one party or the other. Only 39% of respondents leaned Republican.

That 10-point spread marks a sharp reversal from the four-point advantage that Republicans held over Democrats in the fourth quarter of 2024, when voters sent Donald Trump back to the White House and Republicans swept both houses of Congress. Democrats are seeing their most sizable advantage since 2008, when Barack Obama was elected president, according to the New York Times.

The data offers the latest evidence that Trump’s second term has proved unpopular with voters, driving a potential backlash.

Trump’s approval rating stood at 52% at the time of his second inauguration in January of 2025, according to an average of polls published by the New York Times.

But his popularity dwindled immediately, as he cleaved the federal workforce, imposed price-inflating tariffs, passed a profligate spending bill and launched a rudderless war with Iran. Some 58% of voters now disapprove of his performance, with only 38% approving, according to the Times.

Democrats are hoping to take advantage of Trump’s tanking popularity. Liberals are likely to retake the US House of Representatives in midterm elections this November. The party is much less certain to retake the US Senate, though polling is giving Democrats reasons to feel optimistic.

A growing share of American voters have not identified with either party in recent years. Back in 2002, roughly a third of voters surveyed by Gallup identified as either Republican, Democrat or independent. By last year, 45% of respondents called themselves independents, with only 27% identifying as either Democrat or Republican.

articles.title: Possums in the roof, koalas in bed: study shows how animals resort to Australian homes after habitat loss
articles.excerpt:
Microbats and wombats among the most common species found in buildings, with some discovered in letter boxes or air conditioning systems

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

P...
articles.body_text:
Microbats and wombats among the most common species found in buildings, with some discovered in letter boxes or air conditioning systems

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Possums in the roof, bats in the curtains and ducks on the balcony: new research has revealed how native animals are making themselves at home in our houses.

Researchers have analysed a decade of wildlife rescue reports and found brushtail and ringtail possums make up half of all cases of animals in buildings, followed by microbats and bare-nosed wombats.

The study in People and Nature included 2,400 cases of animals using buildings as habitat. Most were found in roof spaces, walls, garages and under the house, although some preferred more unusual locations like letterboxes or air conditioning systems. About 10% were found in indoor rooms such as bedrooms and kitchens.

Bethany Kiss, a University of Melbourne architect and the lead author of the study, said animals were seeking out buildings as substitute habitats as their natural homes and hollows disappeared.

“We found native wildlife using almost every part of the house imaginable,” Kiss said. “People often think these are unusual incidents, but they’re actually very common.”

Wildlife Victoria, which provided the data for the study, said one recent caller to its emergency response service discovered juvenile sugar gliders in her kitchen.

“She had reached under the sink for a dishwashing tablet and instead her hand landed on something furry,” said Aleisha Hall, a spokesperson for the rescue organisation. Investigating further, they found two gliders curled up together in a small jar.

When a volunteer was dispatched to collect the gliders, they found five more.

In another recent case, an echidna found its way into a house and headed straight for the pantry. “The homeowner found him pulling items off the shelves, including a heavy food processor,” Hall said.

Luckily, the homeowner was also a wildlife rescuer and was able to safely return it back outside.

Microbats often featured in calls to Wildlife Victoria’s hotline. Recently, while renovating, a homeowner found eight little forest bats roosting in a wall.

Ericka Tudhope, a rehabilitation specialist from Microbats of Melbourne, said bats living in the roof was common and nothing to be concerned about – so long as people left them alone and didn’t touch them.

“They make great housemates by keeping bug numbers down and rarely do any damage to the house. They don’t chew cables or wires,” she said.

In New South Wales, the Wires rescue service said animals often sought shelter during cold or extreme weather.

Last year a member of the public rang when a koala scampered down her hallway. By the time the rescue volunteer arrived, the animal was sitting calmly on her bed.

While such cohabiting in Australian houses was mostly accidental, in the United Kingdom buildings were being intentionally designed for habitat, Kiss said, such as the requirement to include “swift nesting bricks” in new builds.

“We’re in a biodiversity crisis and a housing crisis,” she said.

While architecture often focused on ways to keep nature out, there were opportunities to design buildings that were better for both people and wildlife. That could include wildlife-friendly lighting and noise reduction measures, as well as habitat features, like swallow shelves or possum boxes.

“One of the things that I would really like to see in Australia, is that we think about embedding the ecologist in the design process like you would with, say, an engineer,” Kiss said.

Prof Sarah Bekessy, a co-author of the paper and Biodiversity Council lead councillor, said research consistently showed that people benefited from everyday interactions with wildlife.

“Wildlife in our neighbourhoods can improve our mental wellbeing, strengthen people’s connection with nature and make cities healthier, more resilient places to live,” she said.

Wildlife Victoria said it advocated for peaceful coexistence where possible, but anyone concerned about an animal in their home was encouraged to contact their local wildlife rescue.

articles.title: Alarming AI ads are flooding social media in the lead-up to Victoria’s election. But who is behind them?
articles.excerpt:
A machete-wielding robber, a ‘tsunami of debt’ … campaigns echoing opposition talking points outspend major parties

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A man clad in a balacl...
articles.body_text:
A machete-wielding robber, a ‘tsunami of debt’ … campaigns echoing opposition talking points outspend major parties

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A man clad in a balaclava and brandishing a machete terrorises a worker at a petrol station before firebombing the building on the way out.

A woman gives birth on the side of the road, unable to reach a hospital due to ambulance ramping and crater-like potholes, which also stop a fire truck in its tracks.

A flood of water – emblematic of Victoria’s “tsunami of debt”, forecast to hit $199bn in the next four years – gushes from the steps of state parliament, towards a scared child.

These are some of the AI-generated images being used as part of a social media advertising campaign attracting thousands of views less than 100 days out from the Victorian election.

According to one expert, the ads, created by a group called Fix Victoria, cost up to $100,000 to publish in August, which is significantly more than most major parties and candidates spent.

Another group, Better Victoria, is also spending big on short ads to pit Labor initiatives – such as the multibillion-dollar Suburban Rail Loop – against investment in roads, schools and hospitals.

But who is behind these groups and are they affiliated with a political party?

Fix Victoria is run by experienced political operatives who held senior positions at a conservative thinktank, the Institute of Public Affairs (IPA). It began plotting its ad campaign in May, when a group of like-minded people started recruiting paying members who could finance its operations and ads.

Corporate filings show it was registered with Asic in early August by Deborah Henderson, who was until June the deputy executive director of the IPA. Its communications director is Andrew Hudgson, who held a similar role at the IPA until earlier this year. Its head of advocacy is Gideon Rozner, who spent six years at the IPA before working at an investment firm.

Fix Victoria is a separate entity to the IPA and its staff say it is coincidence that three of them previously worked at the thinktank, which is a long-term critic of Labor governments.

In November, Rozner told his social media followers that he was rejoining the Liberal party to support its new leader, Jess Wilson.

“The best place for me is to stand with the thousands of Victorians who will get around Jess Wilson to defeat this disgusting Labor government and save the great state of Victoria,” Rozner posted on X.

When asked by Guardian Australia whether he is still a member of the Liberal party, Rozner declines to answer but says: “I’ve been around for a long time – and my views and affiliations are well-known.”

Rozner says Fix Victoria is an “issues-driven, not politics-driven” organisation that wants to “ensure our leaders know that everyday Victorians want a plan to get out of the mess we are currently in”.

“Fix Victoria is focused on the three key issues dragging our state down, that being crime, corruption and debt,” Rozner says.

These three issues happen to be key talking points of opposition parties.

“Victoria’s tsunami of debt steals resources from policing so organised illegal tobacco criminals are making billions, recruiting vulnerable kids and making our streets unsafe,” one 30-second Fix Victoria ad says.

A loophole in Victoria’s electoral laws means voters may never know who is ultimately funding these ads.

Groups publishing political ads during campaigns don’t need to be registered as third-party campaigners unless they specifically promote or oppose a party or a candidate.

The Centre for Public Integrity’s executive director, Catherine Williams, says Victoria’s laws are narrower in scope than their federal equivalent.

“Unless an entity meets the definition of third party campaigner, no disclosure obligations apply,” Williams says.

During the federal election campaign, mandatory donation disclosures by one third-party campaign group revealed it had been bankrolled by the coal lobby. The group had been attacking Labor, Greens and independent candidates.

Transparency International Australia’s chief executive, Clancy Moore, says while Fix Victoria does not meet the legal threshold of a third-party campaign group, its ads are “clearly trying to influence voting”.

“It’s really important Victorians know who is behind these types of campaigns and what their political affiliations might be,” Moore says. “There is a long history of third-party and fake grassroots campaign groups exploiting loopholes in electoral laws to try to influence elections.”

Rozner says Fix Victoria has “invested considerable resources to ensure strict compliance with all relevant laws, in particular the Victorian Electoral Act”.

By avoiding reference to political parties or candidates, Fix Victoria’s financial backers are shielded from public view unless disclosed by the group itself.

“We place a very high priority on protecting the security and privacy of our members and supporters,” Rozner says.

Better Victoria was formed a month after Fix Victoria, with its first ads running on Facebook in early August. Its political content is endorsed by the group itself, rather than a office holder.

Listings with Consumer Affairs Victoria show its secretary is Ronald Holzer, a lawyer based in the Melbourne suburb of Caulfied North. Holzer says he only has an administrative role with the group.

He referred a series of questions from Guardian Australia to an unnamed spokesperson, who declined to say who was running the organisation.

“Better Victoria has obtained independent legal advice regarding its activities,” the spokesperson said. “It is confident that its activities are fully compliant with Victoria’s electoral laws.”

The spokesperson said the group had no relationship with any political party and was fully financed by donations from its members. Those donors will also remain hidden.

“Our members include people from a range of backgrounds and professions, who have exercised their right to privacy,” the spokesperson said.

An advertising executive, Ed Coper, who worked with Climate 200 and some teal candidates during the 2025 federal election, says the two groups are spending big.

Coper’s agency, Populares, has tracked their spending using public data and says they spent more on Google and Meta ads than any other state election candidate or party in August.

He says Fix Victoria spent just under $100,000 on ads, which was about a quarter of all the advertising spend related to the election. Better Victoria spent about $40,000.

The two groups also outspent the Liberals, teal independents and One Nation on social media advertising, according to Populares.

Then there’s the ad Fix Victoria ran in the middle of the AFL wildcard final between the Western Bulldogs and Collingwood on Channel Seven on 28 August.

“They will have spent tens of thousands of dollars,” Coper says. “The actual content of their advertising is very, very similar to the way that a political operative will message during an election campaign.”

The country star and mom-of-four tells Fox News Digital keeping kids active and offline is what works for her family.

Jessie James Decker is flaunting her fitness transformation.

While the country singer has always been in shape, she took to social media this week to share a variety of photos and videos of her new, more toned look – including before and after bikini photos.

"This past week in the Hamptons, a woman complimented my arms and said, 'Gosh, I could probably never have arms like yours,'" Decker wrote. "I looked at her and said, 'Girl, I didn’t have these arms in April!'"

HILARIA BALDWIN FLAUNTS FIT FIGURE IN BIKINI AS FANS MARVEL AT MOM OF 7

She said that while she's at the same weight she was then, she's been working hard on building muscle and being more consistent, thanks to her JJD Fit app.

"This is the most consistent I have EVER been, and I feel stronger and better than ever and I’m NOT stopping," she wrote.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Jessie James Decker showed off her fitness transformation in before and aft bikini photos. (Danielle Del Valle/Getty Images for Eberjey)

Decker added, "I wanted to share these photos because, of course, I know I looked good on the left, but I feel better on the right. I feel stronger and energized. I feel proud of myself. I feel like I’m taking care of me!!"

She explained that very day, she takes 30 minutes to herself, saying, "That little bit of time makes me a better mom and a better person."

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

"I made a promise to myself…and I don’t break promises to me."

Her hard work seems to be paying off in multiple ways – in another video she shared this week, she effortlessly lifted her husband, former NFL star Eric Decker, onto their kitchen counter.

Jessie James Decker has been married to Eric Decker for 13 years. (Jessie James Decker Instagram)

Earlier this year, Jessie told Fox News Digital about how important it is to her family – she and Eric share four children – to be active together.

"We’ve done family workouts together, but we stay active together," she said. "Maybe when we’re on vacation, we’re doing bike rides together, or whether it’s like a football game outside or throwing the ball on the beach."

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

One sport, in particular, has become a family favorite.

Jessie James Decker attends the 60th Academy of Country Music Awards at the Ford Center at The Star on May 8, 2025, in Frisco, Texas. (Gilbert Flores/Penske Media via Getty Images)

"We love pickleball. That’s probably the thing that we all do every day," she said. "We have a pickleball court in the backyard, and if we go on vacation, my husband’s like, ‘Is there a pickleball court at this place?’"

About her children, she said, "They’re active. That’s all I can say. They are busy, busy, busy. They don’t sit around on iPads. They’re out there in the wildlife, barefoot and being free."

Fox News Digital's Stephanie Giang-Paunon contributed to this report.

Emily Trainham is an entertainment editor for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Indiana's mascot starts the season with an absolute heater that puts other mascots to shame
articles.excerpt:
The Big Noon Kickoff crew discuss whether Indiana is now a perennial National Championship contender.

The Indiana Hoosiers began their quest to build on a magical 2025 season that ended with a nation...
articles.body_text:
The Big Noon Kickoff crew discuss whether Indiana is now a perennial National Championship contender.

The Indiana Hoosiers began their quest to build on a magical 2025 season that ended with a national championship.

It remains to be seen how the year will turn out, but one thing is already certain: their mascot, Hoosier the Bison, will be bringing it every single weekend.

The Hoosiers reintroduced a bison mascot for the first time in sixty years last season, and the timing proved to be perfect.

MINOR LEAGUE PLAYER GETS SMOKED BY A SCOOTER-RIDING MASCOT IN WILD MOMENT CAUGHT ON CAMERA

Hoosier the Bison, the Indiana Hoosiers' mascot, is on quite the run since debuting last season. (Photo by CFP/Getty Images))

For his debut, Hoosier skydived into Memorial Stadium.

Ripping a speed star like Keanu and Patrick Swayze in "Point Break" is tough to beat for a mascot debut. It was easily the best since Gritty threatened to kill the Penguins mascot.

So, for his sophomore season, Hoosier went with the zip line.

But if that was the extent of the mascottery, it left a little on the table.

I'm being told he also drove around the field in an IndyCar while the marching band performed.

HERE'S WHY, EVEN WITH ALL ITS PROBLEMS, COLLEGE FOOTBALL IS STILL BETTER THAN THE NFL

That's one of those "The European mind can't comprehend it" moments.

"Why is that cow driving a racecar on the pitch while the band is playing?"

First of all, it's a "bison" and a "field," and secondly, it's because it's college football, Üter.

What a start. I love to see restraint like that on display. Hoosier didn't have to knock everyone's proverbial socks off with the zip line because he knew that there was an open-wheel race car waiting in the wings.

Hoosier the Bison kicked off Indiana's 2026 campaign by driving an IndyCar onto the field. (Photo by Brian Spurlock/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

You don't see that out of these modern mascots; usually only the blue bloods have the experience to know that you don't want to give away everything with your opener.

Fortunately, mascots aren't getting poached by way of NIL (not yet, but give it time) because after that performance, there's no doubt some schools with big checkbooks would be circling him like sharks around fresh chum.

articles.title: Somehow, the Miami Hurricanes have done it again with yet another Heisman-level quarterback
articles.excerpt: "Yeah, heading into Monday night brother Florida State SMU, big ole game Monday night, Labor Day, wrapping up the weekend. This could be the swan song. Not in the best possible way for Mike Norvell. I...
articles.body_text:
"Yeah, heading into Monday night brother Florida State SMU, big ole game Monday night, Labor Day, wrapping up the weekend. This could be the swan song. Not in the best possible way for Mike Norvell. If Kevin Jennings rolls in the Tallahassee you know and they're throwing up 400 yards and four touchdowns, you can go ahead and start putting that Mike Norvell buyout plan together."

January 13, 2024. I was at a friend's birthday party with a group of fans representing each of the "Big 3" Florida schools (Miami, Florida, and Florida State).

Being a Gator fan, I was relishing in joining my fellow Florida fanatics and Seminole supporters mocking the Miami contingent that they had whiffed on all their quarterback targets in the transfer portal.

ACC SUPREMACY: IS IT REALLY THE MIAMI HURRICANES VERSUS THE FIELD FOR THE 2026 SEASON?

As we laughed and reveled in their misery, a notification flashed across everyone's phone screen that changed the tide of the night in favor of the Canes fans.

"BREAKING: Cam Ward, the ex-Washington State QB, heading to Miami."

ONE OF THESE EIGHT COLLEGE FOOTBALL TEAMS WILL BE HOISTING THE NATIONAL CHAMPIONSHIP TROPHY IN 2026

Nov 9, 2024; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Miami Hurricanes quarterback Cam Ward (1) on the sideline against the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets in the first quarter at Bobby Dodd Stadium at Hyundai Field. (Brett Davis-Imagn Images)

The Hurricanes had found their guy, but after a Heisman-level season in 2024, their one year rental was off to the NFL Draft.

So Miami's rivals fired up the trolls once again, and towards the end of the portal period, it looked like the Hurricanes were going to have to eat crow.

That is, until they plucked Georgia quarterback Carson Beck from the ranks of the NFL Draft.

Then the Canes rode another late transfer pickup to within a quarter of winning the national championship.

So when Miami and Mario Cristobal were without a signal caller heading into the teeth of the offseason, we all knew better than to gloat.

And that proved to be the right decision, as the Canes once again persuaded an NFL Draft hopeful - this time Duke transfer Darian Mensah - to hop in the boat in Coral Gables.

UCLA QUARTERBACK ATTEMPTS TO EXPLOIT LOOPHOLE IN TRANSFER PORTAL WINDOW WITH UNIQUE TACTIC

Darian Mensah, No. 10, of the Miami (FL) Hurricanes passes the ball against the Stanford Cardinal in the first half at Stanford Stadium in Stanford, Calif., on Sept. 4, 2026. (Getty Images)

Mensah was given a king's ransom to make his way down to South Florida, and so far, though it's only been one game, that investment is looking to be paying dividends.

I think I speak for the rest of college football when I ask: how do the Canes keep doing this?

COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S AP TOP 25 IS OUT: WHO’S OVERRATED, UNDERRATED AND FLAT-OUT SNUBBED?

I'm reminded of the famous scene from "Breaking Bad," when Aaron Paul's character screams "HE CAN'T KEEP GETTING AWAY WITH IT!"

Granted, Miami played a Stanford team that was missing half its roster due to injury and probably isn't much to write home about even when fully healthy.

But those numbers would look good in a 7-on-7 scrimmage, let alone in a conference game on the road three time zones from home.

Mensah looked as good as the numbers suggested, too, ripping NFL-level throws and distributing the ball to his myriad playmakers, namely wide receiver Malachi Toney.

Somehow, some way, Cristobal and the Canes have another quarterback who can realistically win the Heisman trophy and lead them on a deep Playoff run.

Head coach Mario Cristobal of the Miami Hurricanes looks on in the fourth quarter against the Ole Miss Rebels during the College Football Playoff Semifinal at the VRBO Fiesta Bowl at State Farm Stadium on Jan. 8, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Christian Petersen/Getty Images)

The schedule for Miami won't offer a ton of resistance either; there will be far more Stanford-level teams than Playoff-caliber ones.

When you combine all that and Mensah's skill with the weapons he's been surrounded with (not to mention elite offensive coordinator Shannon Dawson), the Hurricanes might be here to stay.

STAY "FEARLESS" ON THE GO! TAKE TOMI LAHREN WITH YOU. DOWNLOAD THE TLIF PODCAST NOW!

Let this be a warning to any rival fanbase rooting on the downfall of Miami (I include myself in that).

If the offseason starts to drag on next January and they still haven't signed a quarterback, don't hit send on that X post with all the laughing emojis.

Chances are they are a few calls away from landing a potential first-rounder looking to give college one last go.

articles.body_text:
Colin McDonald, the fraud czar and assistant attorney general for the Fraud Division, details the FBI's 'Most Wanted Fraudsters' list. He emphasizes that the time for these individuals to hide in the dark is over, as their identities and alleged multi-million dollar schemes are now being exposed to the public.

FIRST ON FOX: The FBI's Most Wanted Fraudsters initiative notched its fifth arrest in just three months after authorities in India arrested Manjit Singh Bedi on Friday, with the bureau now working to return the alleged SNAP benefits fraud suspect to the United States, Fox News Digital has learned.

The FBI worked with Indian authorities to secure Bedi's arrest and is actively working to return him to the U.S. to face charges, according to the bureau. Bedi's arrest marks the fifth under the FBI's Most Wanted Fraudsters initiative, which targets fugitives accused of major financial crimes.

Launched in June, the initiative has led to the arrests of five fugitives whom the FBI says are collectively accused of more than $2 billion in alleged fraud after spending nearly 4,000 combined days on the run.

FBI NABS ALLEGED $547M MEDICARE FRAUD FUGITIVE OVERSEAS, THIRD CAPTURE FROM 'MOST WANTED FRAUDSTERS' LIST

An undated FBI photo shows Manjit Singh Bedi, who investigators allege defrauded the U.S. government out of at least $600,000 through a SNAP benefits fraud scheme before fleeing to India. (FBI)

FBI officials say the latest arrest underscores the bureau's effort to pursue alleged fraudsters who fled overseas in an attempt to evade prosecution.

"Five Most Wanted Fraudsters captured in just three months is a historic success for this initiative," FBI Director Kash Patel told Fox News Digital.

Patel said the five suspects are allegedly responsible for more than $2 billion in fraud and spent nearly 4,000 combined days on the run before their arrests.

"The days of taking advantage of American taxpayers without consequence are over," Patel said.

Federal investigators allege Bedi defrauded the U.S. government out of at least $600,000 through a Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) fraud scheme between March 2024 and June 2025, while operating an Asian grocery store in Tacoma, Washington.

EXCLUSIVE: FBI ADDS ALLEGED COVID FRAUDSTER ACCUSED OF TAKING $5M FROM KIDS' MEAL PROGRAM TO MOST WANTED LIST

The FBI had offered a reward of up to $150,000 for information leading to Bedi's arrest and conviction. (Ronaldo Bolaños / Los Angeles Times via Getty Images, File)

According to the FBI, Bedi allegedly swiped SNAP recipients' Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) cards, gave them cash instead of eligible food purchases and kept roughly half of the benefits for himself.

After being indicted on wire fraud and SNAP benefits fraud charges, Bedi was ordered to surrender his passport and remain in Washington state while awaiting court proceedings, according to the FBI.

Investigators allege he instead drove across the Canadian border before fleeing to India. A federal arrest warrant charging him with violating the conditions of his release was issued on May 21, 2026.

The FBI had offered a reward of up to $150,000 for information leading to Bedi's arrest and conviction. The bureau said the naturalized U.S. citizen was believed to be living in India before his arrest.

Manjit Singh Bedi is seen in an undated FBI photo. Authorities arrested Bedi in India on Friday after alleging he fled the United States while facing wire fraud and SNAP benefits fraud charges. (FBI)

"As this arrest in India shows, the Justice Department's reach extends to every corner of the planet," Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department's National Fraud Enforcement Division told Fox News Digital.

"The Fraud Division will continue to work hand-in-hand with the FBI to ensure fraudsters like Bedi are held accountable, no matter where they hide."

The FBI said it is working to return Bedi to the U.S. to face the pending charges.

Brittany Miller is a Fox News Digital breaking news writer and former Independent reporter who graduated from Syracuse University in 2023.

articles.title: Former Pentagon AI chief warns Flock cameras could create 'China-like surveillance state' in the US
articles.excerpt: Former Pentagon A.I. Policy Director Mark Beall discusses the growing debate over Flock Safety cameras and classroom AI bans. Beall addresses privacy concerns surrounding automated surveillance and an...
articles.body_text:
Former Pentagon A.I. Policy Director Mark Beall discusses the growing debate over Flock Safety cameras and classroom AI bans. Beall addresses privacy concerns surrounding automated surveillance and analyzes the decision by New York City and Los Angeles schools to restrict artificial intelligence. He also shares insights on how AI developments could impact classical education.

Former Pentagon AI Policy Director Mark Beall warned that expanding artificial intelligence surveillance tools, like Flock cameras, could turn American communities into a "China-like surveillance state" unless guardrails are enforced.

Speaking on "Saturday in America," Beall argued that while this technology can have vital law enforcement benefits, clear rules and judicial oversight are necessary to protect the rights of Americans at home.

"We have to be careful that we don't go too far to the other direction and create a China-like surveillance state, which is literally what AI capabilities will ultimately enable and are enabling right now," Beall told Fox News.

TEENS ACCUSED OF DESTROYING FLOCK CAMERA UNTIL BATTERY EXPLODED, IGNITING FIRE NEAR HOMES: REPORT

Members of the Muslim Justice League and other activists march toward Flock Safety offices during a protest on Aug. 19, 2026, in Boston, Mass. The demonstration came amid scrutiny of the company's license plate camera technology and its use by law enforcement. (Barry Chin/The Boston Globe via Getty Images)

From destroyed camera poles to viral signs blocking surveillance lenses, some communities are pushing back against neighborhood surveillance cameras. Flock cameras are automated license plate readers used by law enforcement to record vehicle data that can aid criminal investigations. People in communities with the cameras have raised concerns about privacy and potential misuse by law enforcement.

Beall acknowledged that the technology can benefit law enforcement but said people’s privacy concerns are also valid. He urged a compromise and called for guardrails on how the cameras can be used, including strict rules and court oversight to prevent officers from abusing the technology for personal reasons.

FLOCK SAFETY CAMERAS NEED CONSTITUTIONAL GUARDRAILS BEFORE FURTHER DEPLOYMENT, TENNESSEE MAYOR ARGUES

"It’s tough to bring the message of compromise to the American people, especially when it comes to our constitutional protections," Beall said.

"I think what we're seeing across the board when it comes to artificial intelligence is that the innovation upside is so tremendous, but across all of these different use cases, including the Flock cameras, what we really need are strong guardrails, a strong policy that allows us to maintain those special values, the American founding principles that make this country so great," he added.

FLOCK SURVEILLANCE SPREADS ACROSS THE SOUTH AS RED-STATE LAWMAKERS SEEK TO AX '1984'-STYLE TRACKING TOOLS

Fox News Digital reached out to Flock Safety for comment, but did not immediately hear back.

A pigeon perches on a Flock Safety camera, mounted high on traffic signal pole at the intersection of Chapman Avenue & Harbor Boulevard in Garden Grove, Calif. on Friday, Aug. 14, 2026. (Allen J. Schaben/Los Angeles Times via Getty Images)

Lawmakers from both parties have raised similar concerns and called for rules governing the surveillance technology. Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., has proposed banning the technology outright, and Rep. Tim Burchett, R-Tenn., has pushed to cut federal funding for local installations.

In Florida, transportation officials have ordered law enforcement agencies to take down the license plate readers from state highways. They cited privacy concerns and reports of misuse of the technology.

DAVID MARCUS: CHINA TRIP A GLIMPSE INTO THE SURVEILLANCE STATE AMERICA MUST NEVER BECOME

Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis criticized the cameras at a news conference Monday, saying, "If you want to get in your car and you want to go down to Buc-ee's in St. Augustine, it's really none of the government's damn business if you're doing that, right? What we don't want in the state of Florida is to have a digital AI surveillance state where everything we're doing is being tracked at all times."

He added that the technology has sometimes been useful but questioned where the data is going and how it is being stored.

"They claim that the companies aren't going to misuse it, but no one's watching that, and I know you can make some money selling cameras, but you really can make a lot of money if you can sell people's data," DeSantis said.

Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis speaks during a press conference at Florida International University alongside Jared Purdue, head of the Florida Division of Emergency Management, on Aug. 26, 2026, in Miami, Fla. (Al Diaz/Miami Herald/Tribune News Service via Getty Images)

THE SURVEILLANCE CAMERA ON YOUR STREET CORNER: LAWFUL SPYING OR CONSTITUTIONALLY PROBLEMATIC?

In August, Flock Safety CEO Garrett Langley addressed privacy and safety concerns in an interview with Fox News host Kayleigh McEnany.

"When people talk about just one of these, privacy or safety, they're prioritizing the wrong thing, and what we have to prioritize as a country is compromise," Langley told Fox News. "How do we have our safety, and how do we balance privacy?"

EX-INDIANA DEPUTY CHARGED WITH FELONY FOR ALLEGEDLY USING FLOCK CAMERAS TO STALK GIRLFRIEND

He said the company is focused on ensuring the technology is used for good, including by recommending seven-day data retention limits and holding those who misuse the system accountable.

"Today, it is too often that in Flock and in other technologies, there's no regulation. There's no accountability, and we think that's wrong," Langley said.

"We announced changes that required auditing, that required using our audit assistance tool, which detects abnormal behavior, and we're calling on state regulators to focus less on banning this type of technology and more [on] holding our law enforcement community accountable," he added.

Madison Colombo is a writer for Fox News Digital’s Flash, Media, and Culture team, covering daily breaking news and trending topics with an award-winning background in broadcast and digital journalism.

articles.title: TV presenter among 11 sentenced to death in Egypt drugs case
articles.excerpt:

Egyptian television presenter Sarah Khalifa and 11 other people have been sentenced to death by hang...
articles.body_text:
Sarah Khalifa is best known for her TV programme Mission Impossible which dealt with crime issues.

Egyptian television presenter Sarah Khalifa and 11 other people have been sentenced to death by hanging after being convicted of drugs charges.

According to state-owned al-Akhram newspaper, they were part of a criminal gang which imported ingredients used to make drugs with the intent of selling them.

They also had illegal firearms and munitions.

Khalifa, 39, is best known for her TV programme Mission Impossible which dealt with crime issues. She has denied the charges.

The verdict - which can be appealed against - was first announced last month.

However, it was only confirmed a month later after the court obtained a religious opinion from the grand mufti of Egypt - a legal requirement in death sentence cases.

During the trial, the court heard that authorities had seized more than 750kg (1,653lbs) of narcotics and the imported raw materials to make them.

Twenty witnesses had given statements to the prosecutors, al-Akhram said, in addition to electronic evidence that included conversations and video clips.

According to the state-run Akhbar al-Youm newspaper, when asked by the judge about her alleged role during a court appearance last September, Khalifa said she had never seen any drugs until she was photographed with them inside the anti-narcotics authority offices.

According to a 2025 Amnesty International report, there were 492 death sentences in the course of the year, 23 of whom were executed, external.

The defendants were found guilty of drug trafficking and rape, "crimes that did not amount to 'intentional killing' to which the use of the death penalty must be restricted under international law and standards", the report said.

articles.body_text:
